News.title: Navy SEALs blew up dozens of deadly Iranian mines in ‘secret, four-month special op mission’ to clear Strait of Hormuz
News.content:
NAVY SEALs embarked on a secret four-month mission to hunt down and blow-up dozens of Iranian mines lurking in the Strait of Hormuz.

The covert US operation saw elite divers plunge into the perilous waterway as they battled to clear the route which is vital to the world’s oil supplies.



Operating largely under the cover of darkness, the SEALs used drones, robotic vessels and high-tech sonar to track down the explosive traps.

The four-month operation was carried out amid a terrifying barrage of strikes between the US and Iran, according to a report by the Financial Times.



It was aimed at reopening the strategic strait to commercial shipping after vessels largely abandoned the treacherous route following US and Israeli attacks on Iran in February.

But even after sophisticated technology has pinpointed suspected mines, the most dangerous job could still fall to a human being.

A retired US Navy captain Bill Hamblet, who often operated in the Gulf, told the FT: “That is usually followed up by a navy diver who’s got to get in the water and approach the mine, and then put a charge on it and destroy it.”

The underwater bomb squad could also unleash robotic drones to approach and destroy the mines with explosives – a safer option for the divers but a painfully slow one.



Among the weapons in the Navy’s technological arsenal was the Common Uncrewed Surface Vessel, or CUSV – a drone boat capable of towing unmanned submersibles through the deadly waters.

One of those, the MK 18 Mod 2 Kingfish, is fitted with sonar technology capable of scanning the ocean floor for suspicious objects.

Despite the treacherous operation, no US casualties have been reported in connection with the mine-clearing mission.

It comes as Iran is accused of plotting a terrifying October 7-style assault on Israel using its sprawling network of terror proxies.

Trump has meanwhile vowed that the bloody conflict will ultimately send oil prices crashing as he insisted Iran will never be allowed to get its hands on a nuclear weapon.



Writing on Truth Social, the US president said: “Oil prices will drop precipitously, like everything else is dropping (but more!), when we WIN the war with Iran.

“Three Dollars a gallon, but ultimately, below Two Dollars a gallon. It will all happen quickly, and Iran will never have a Nuclear Weapon. MAGA! President DJT”.

Israeli intelligence has reportedly claimed Tehran has held meetings and training exercises with Hezbollah, Hamas, the Houthis and Iraqi militias as it looks to bolster its forces and weapons stockpiles.



It comes as US forces launched a blistering attack on three Iranian oil tankers last week after Tehran reportedly fired missiles at American warships.

US Central Command said it “permanently disabled” two tankers and “completely destroyed” a third, claiming the vessels were part of a shadow network funnelling cash to Iran’s Revolutionary Guard and its armed proxies.

The scale of the underwater menace was laid bare in June when the United Nations’ International Maritime Organization estimated that around 80 mines had been planted along the Strait.

The strategic waterway handles around 20 per cent of the world’s oil transports, making the explosive threat a potential nightmare for global energy supplies.

Iran has repeatedly claimed its mines remain active in the Strait and its military has claimed two attacks on oil tankers in the past week.



US President Donald Trump last week declared that “all mines” in the international waters of the Strait had been removed or destroyed.

The US military subsequently confirmed the claim.

But fears of a fresh Iranian mining blitz have continued to stalk ships attempting the dangerous crossing.



The threat has also sparked fierce uncertainty among shipping firms over whether the entire waterway is truly safe.

Shipping companies and maritime analysts believe areas close to the Omani coast – where US forces have been escorting ships – are likely to have been cleared.

But there is far less certainty over the rest of the Strait.

“It’s hard to know what to believe,” Ethan Connell, assistant director of Taiwan Security Monitor and an expert on mines, told the FT.

“Iran is certainly trying to re-mine.”



The latest mine scare comes as the Strait has been hammered by missile and drone attacks, sending visible shipping traffic crashing to its lowest level since May, according to maritime intelligence firm Kpler.

Just two ships crossed the Strait on Saturday, while only six made the perilous journey on Sunday.

Most of those vessels travelled through a route approved by Iran.

But the true scale of traffic remains shrouded in mystery, with some ships reportedly switching off their transponders and creeping through the Strait under the protection of US military escorts.

The danger facing the crews is compounded by the sheer difficulty of hunting mines beneath the waves while a war rages around them.



The secret mission involved small teams of Navy divers operating from inflatable-hulled boats, backed by unmanned surface vessels and specialised underwater equipment.

Sonar-equipped submersibles were used to scour the seabed for suspected explosives before the dangerous process of destroying them began.

And despite the robotic technology, some mines still had to be tackled at close quarters by Navy divers.

The painstaking operation amounted to an underwater bomb disposal mission carried out in the middle of a war zone.

“It is an extremely time-consuming process,” said Nitya Labh, an associate fellow at Chatham House.



“They are doing, essentially, active bomb detonation underwater.”

The mission was carried out despite a twist that raised fresh questions over the US mine-clearing effort.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Three American vessels normally assigned to mine-countermeasure operations in the Gulf had reportedly been operating in the Indian and Pacific oceans since at least early June.

Mine clearance is already a notoriously slow and dangerous business in peacetime.

News.title: Protesters ‘launched rocks & bricks’ at police during anti-migrant clashes in Portsmouth after ‘catching cops off guard’
News.content:
PROTESTERS have been accused of launching rocks and bricks at cops who were “caught off guard” during anti-migrant clashes on Sunday.

Around 200 people – some wearing face coverings – descended on Eastney ferry port in Portsmouth after 140 migrants were brought to shore.



Several vans and cars were reportedly damaged as multiple officers were injured during the chaos which went deep into the night.

Cops guarded coaches parked on a roadside not far from the marina, as protesters blocked the flow of traffic and stopped RNLI teams from accessing the port.



Policing Minister Sarah Jones told the House of Commons that the chaos was “intimidating and thuggish”.

She said protesters would face the “full force of the law”.





The migrant boat from Normandy which sparked the chaos was thought to have been the longest-ever Channel crossing by people smugglers.

It was intercepted in the Solent between the Isle of Wight and Portsmouth earlier on Sunday.

Portsmouth City Council said the Home Office had “serious questions to answer” over the decision to bring migrants to shore in the area.

Council leader Steve Pitt said the move had caused “needless disruption”.



In a statement, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said a number of officers were treated at the scene for injuries, none of which were serious.

It said: “Violence and criminal damage have no part in peaceful protest.

“No arrests have been made at this time, however an investigation to identify offenders responsible for any assaults to officers, criminal damage to vehicles or other criminal offences has been launched.”

Spencer Wragg, chair of Hampshire Police Federation, said: “I’ve seen footage of officers being pushed off their motorbikes, I’ve seen pictures of police vehicles damaged.



“It appears that the police last night became the target for some of the protest.”

Border Force confirmed that the coaches leaving the dock in the early hours of Monday were transporting “individuals from the boat” for “processing”.

Protesters claim they were trying to stop authorities from ferrying migrants to the Manston centre in Kent.

Reform leader Nigel Farage said the country was on the precipice of “serious civil disturbance” and called on the protests to remain peaceful.

Posting to social media, he said: “Peaceful protest: good. Uniforms and masks: bad. Voting is the only way we get a solution.”



His remarks prompted Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo, to urge the Reform leader to be “careful” with his words.

Livestreaming the mayhem, the far-right figure had called on his supporters to “get down to Eastney”.

Danny later barged into the frame during a Sky News interview with Reform’s spokesperson for home affairs, Zia Yusuf.

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp also condemned the violence in Portsmouth.

But he added: “This should also be a wake-up call for the government because it’s not just those protesters in Dover and Portsmouth who feel so angry about large-scale illegal immigration.



“It is millions and millions of people up and down this country who feel angry as well.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It follows a similar incident on Saturday, which saw some 625 masked men assemble at the Port of Dover to protest against small-boat crossings.

A total of 16,513 people arrived in the UK on small boats up until September 1, 43 per cent less than the same period the previous year.

News.title: Elderly woman, 80, forced to lie on the ground for over FOUR hours as she waited for ambulance after nasty fall
News.content:
OAP'S TORMENT Elderly woman, 80, forced to lie on the ground for over FOUR hours as she waited for ambulance after nasty fall

AN ELDERLY woman was forced to lie on the pavement for more than four hours as she waited for an ambulance after suffering a nasty fall.

Kathleen Bryson, 80, was pictured on the ground wrapped up in blankets after concerned neighbours rushed to the OAP’s side.



Kathleen fell outside her home in County Durham at 11.20am on Monday morning and was unable to move due to her age and the pain from the landing.

At 3.30pm, she was still lying in almost the exact same position on the pavement waiting for medical help.



Speaking to ChronicleLive at the time, Kathleen’s son, Karl Bryson, said: “It’s been nearly three hours that she’s been lying on the concrete floor.

“She’s just lying there in the same position. She’s 80 years old.”



Karl was doing some gardening work when he received a call from his sister saying their mum had had a fall.

They believe she may have tripped on a pothole in the pavement.

When he arrived, neighbours had already contacted the North East Ambulance Service and Karl waited almost an hour before calling back at 12.10pm.

When no ambulance had arrived by 2pm, Karl and a neighbour called back for an update.



At this point the wait had exceeded two hours, which he says he was told would be the maximum time Kathleen would have to wait.

However, the pain continued until 3.34pm when an ambulance eventually arrived on scene to assist Kathleen, according to service logs.

Vicky Court, deputy chief operating officer for North East Ambulance Service, said: “We are sorry for the delay experienced by Ms Bryson and for the distress this has caused her and her family.

“We recognise that Ms Bryson waited far longer than we would like and this is not the service we would have wanted to provide for her.

“Our teams work hard to respond to patients as quickly as possible, but at times of high demand, our resources must always be prioritised by clinical need for patients whose lives are immediately in danger.



“We will review this incident and would encourage Ms Bryson or her family to contact our patient experience team through our formal complaints process so that the circumstances can be fully investigated and we can feed back to her directly.”

News.title: Moment police ram driver, 35, off road and cuff him after 3 week ‘crime spree’ saw thief steal cars, coffee & whiskey
News.content:
THIS is the moment police ram a driver in a stolen car off the road and finally end his three week “crime spree”.

Liam McDonald, 35, was handcuffed and later jailed for a number of offences, including stealing two cars, five jars of coffee, and two bottles of whiskey.



Video footage shows the disqualified driver swerving through lanes in Cardiff after being confronted head-on by police.

Officers were searching for a stolen car when it was spotted driving towards them in July.



Despite McDonald attempting to escape, officers were eventually able to box in the car and safely arrest the man.

McDonald, of no fixed abode, committed several crimes in and around Cardiff across three weeks in July.

After being arrested, he was linked to earlier offences, including stealing five jars of coffee from inside a B&M in Leckwith.

A few days earlier, a different car was reported stolen from an address in Cardiff.



Following CCTV enquiries, a man on a bike – now known to be McDonald – was identified as being responsible for stealing the car.

McDonald then stole two bottles of whiskey worth £119 from a Waitrose in Pontprennau on July 21.

He previously pleaded guilty to numerous offences, including two counts of driving while disqualified, aggravated vehicle taking and dangerous driving, and using a vehicle without third-party insurance.

On Friday, McDonald was sentenced to a year and nine months at Cardiff Crown Court.

He was also banned from driving for three years.



Investigating officer PC Paul Griffiths said: “McDonald committed a spate of offences that had a big impact on the people and businesses in his communities.

“He also put people on the road at risk that day driving in the manner that he did and without a license. I’m pleased to see this sentence handed down today.”

News.title: US accuses Labour of ‘censorship’ over plans to force social media giants to promote ‘trustworthy’ news outlets
News.content:
THE US has accused Labour of seeking to punish critical media outlets with “viewpoint-based censorship”.

Donald Trump’s administration condemned the Government’s plans to force social media sites to promote only news providers deemed “trustworthy”.



The plans would require tech platforms to make stories from public service media such as the BBC more prominent.

The US embassy in London responded by saying: “A framework that empowers governments to influence which sources receive preferential visibility risks becoming a mechanism for viewpoint-based censorship.



“If the UK compels platforms to boost government-preferred media in algorithmic feeds, the effect on a government- disfavoured speaker or media source’s reach is not meaningfully different than ­outright removal.

“Furthermore, such a mandate could establish a template authoritarian regimes could invoke to justify more control over online content.”



PM Andy Burnham is hoping to meet the President for the first time at the United Nations General Assembly later this month.

The News Media Association, which represents the media industry, lashed out at the plans for the government to define which outlets are trustworthy.

It said: “This would be incompatible with a free press, and represent press regulation by the back door.”

A DCMS spokesperson said: “We welcome engagement and responses to our media green paper.



“We believe strongly in free expression and fair competition, and any action we take will ensure these are protected.”

News.title: Fury as UN reveals migrants are being granted asylum in Britain even when they may NOT be entitled to it
News.content:
MIGRANTS are being granted asylum even when they may not be entitled to it, UN investigators have warned.

A probe by the organisation’s Refugee Agency found serious flaws in Home Office interviews used to decide who is allowed to stay in the UK.



Officials warned rushed questioning meant asylum was at risk of being wrongly granted to people who do not qualify — while genuine refugees could be rejected.

UN officials examined 60 interviews and cases and found the full basis of an applicant’s claim was still unclear after questioning in nearly a third of interviews studied.



They uncovered a “failure to probe material facts”, too many closed questions and interpreters summarising migrants’ answers instead of translating them fully.

They warned this created a “real risk” of genuine refugees being rejected while others were granted asylum despite not qualifying.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “The UN — hardly a hostile witness — has told the Home Office that it is granting asylum to people who are not entitled to it.

“Last year alone 58,000 people were granted asylum or leave to remain, a ten per cent increase on the year before, and the highest number of initial decisions since records began.”

Meanwhile, a Government whistleblower has claimed just one in 100 asylum claims are genuine and many “use the same script”.

The Home Office insider, who has assessed thousands of applications, said he and his colleagues have encountered hundreds of Iraqi Kurds purporting to be in a relationship with the daughter of Kurdistan’s prime minister.



The number is so high that it has allegedly become a “running joke” among officials.

He also told The Times that hundreds of Pakistanis claim to fear for their lives because they are in a gay relationship with the same man.

Multiple claims feature photos of “topless guys in a club with their arms around each other trying to prove they’re gay”.

News.title: Andy Burnham braced for Donald Trump clash as he prepares to hit Israel with sanctions
News.content:
ANDY Burnham is bracing for a fresh row with Donald Trump as he prepares to unveil Israeli sanctions as soon as today.

The PM is expected to impose a punishment package on Benjamin Netanyahu’s government over illegal West Bank settlements.



Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is expected to make the announcement today as Labour seeks to win back pro-Gaza voters it has lost in recent years.

But it risks a backlash from the Americans who are understood to be furious with Britain’s hardening approach against Israel.



Washington’s ambassador to Israel recently blasted Labour for being consumed with “Jew hate”.

Mike Huckabee said: “The Brits have lost it.



“The Jew hate of their government knows no boundaries and knows no facts.”

A Number 10 spokesperson completely rejected the claim.

They said: “We’re committed to protecting Jewish communities in the UK, and continue to engage with community leaders and groups.

“The government is investing almost £318 million over three years to protect Jewish communities, crack down on antisemitic extremism and hostile state activity, and tackle antisemitism in schools, universities, and local communities.”



Mr Trump and Mr Burnham spoke last night about the Israel-Gaza war.

A Downing Street spokesman said: “On the Middle East, the Prime Minister set out the UK’s commitment to working towards peace and security in the region, stressing the importance of the Two-State Solution, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and ensuring that Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon.”

News.title: Brit hols hotspot dubbed ‘Devil’s Island’ as 88 of Italy’s most dangerous mafia bosses and terrorists moved to new jail
News.content:
DOZENS of Italy’s most notorious mafia bosses and terrorists have been moved to a jail in a Brit holiday hotspot sparking serious safety concerns.

The group of 88 notorious and hardened criminals have been sent to a new high security wing at Uta prison which has been dubbed “Devil’s Island”.



The criminals are among 746 inmates who are forced to follow Italy‘s strictest solitary confinement rules known as 41-bis.

Prisoners held under these terms are forbidden from talking to each other – limiting their ability to run gang operations from behind bars.



The crooks were transferred to the island on two ATR 42 jets owned by Italian police.

Only eight or nine were allowed to board each flight at a time so cops could prevent communication due to many of the cons’ links to organised crime.

Sardinia’s governor Alessandra Todde blasted the move when it was announced as she warned it posed a risk to the island’s safety.

The latest transfer of inmates has nearly doubled the number of 41-bis prisoners in the island to 183 – about a quarter of the national total.



Todde said: “The government has moved in a unilateral and arrogant way, treating Sardinia like the Cayenne of Italy.”

The Cayenne prison – also nicknamed “Devil’s Island” – was run by France off the coast of French Guiana before being closed in 1953.

Earlier this year, hundreds of protesters swarmed the streets of Cagliari, the Sardinian capital, to demonstrate against the looming arrivals.



Todde warned the island’s jails are already understaffed – a factor which was magnified by the escape of a Puglia mafia boss from one of its jails in 2023.

Prisoners are being sent to Uta jail as part of a plan to concentrate inmates serving life sentences into a smaller number of jails, one prison officer told The Times.

He said the law favoured them being sent to islands to keep them isolated.

The officer said: “We can’t send them to Sicily because many of them come from there in the first place.”

Italy‘s junior justice minister Alberto Balboni called Todde, who represents the opposition party, a hypocrite.



She said: “The new wing of Uta jail for these prisoners was ordered by a minister in a previous government who belonged to the [opposition] Five Star party.”

Balboni argued claims that families of mafia prisoners would move to Sardinia to be closer to their relatives were baseless.

She added: “They do not do this since you can only visit prisoners once a month for a few minutes.”

In the 1990s, Sardinia started to host more and more mob prisoners following a crackdown on Cosa Nostra, the Sicilian mafia.

Many criminals were jailed on the small island of Asinara – nicknamed the Alcatraz of Italy – off Sardinia’s coast.



This included Raffaele Cutolo, a crime boss from Naples, and Salvatore “Toto” Riina, the head of Cosa Nostra.

Toto was linked to 150 killings and orchestrated the murder of anti-mafia officials Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino in 1992.

Asinara only saw one prisoner escape from its facilities during its 112 years of service before it closed in 1997.

The 41-bis system is designed to entice prisoners to give up mafia secrets in return for better living conditions.

Some human rights groups have criticised the standard of living.



Inmates are locked in nine-square-metre cells for 23 hours per day – only being allowed 60 minutes outside for exercise in a tiny yard.

Conversations are closely monitored by prison guards who are familiar with codes used by mafia heads.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Officers also have to make sure bosses who mix don’t kill each other.

The prison source added: “You don’t want mafiosi from the same organisations together but if they are from opposing clans they might try to kill each other.”

News.title: King Charles keeps pace with public engagements despite continuing cancer treatment
News.content:
King Charles keeps pace with public engagements despite continuing cancer treatment

The King has been determined to not slow down during a busy last 12 months, including public duties across the UK and internationally including his historic state visit to the United States

View 3 Images The King with his family on the Buckingham Palace balcony (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

King Charles has proved once again that illness will not slow him down, carrying out engagements on 164 days during the fourth year of his reign - all while continuing treatment for cancer.

‌



The King, now 77, has kept up a punishing schedule despite the diagnosis first announced by Buckingham Palace in February 2024. Far from retreating from public life, he has pressed on with audiences, visits and state occasions throughout his treatment, even through the months in early 2024 when illness kept him largely out of view.

‌



That determination was on full display on the world stage earlier this year, when in late April and early May 2026, Charles undertook a state visit to the United States followed by a tour of Bermuda, his first as sovereign to a British Overseas Territory.

‌



View 3 Images King Charles was joined by Queen Camilla on their historic State Visit to the United States this year (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

While in Washington he became only the second reigning British monarch in history to address Congress, delivering a well-received speech celebrating Anglo-American relations. It capped a remarkable seven months in which he met President Trump twice, first at Windsor Castle last September and then again on American soil.

‌



Months earlier, in October 2025, the King made a two-day state visit to the Vatican, where he met Pope Leo XIV and attended a service in the Sistine Chapel - another sign that neither cancer nor his advancing years have dimmed his appetite for duty. Back home, his 164 days of engagements mark a dip from the 176 recorded the previous year, but represent a rise on both his first year on the throne (161) and his second (133) - a trajectory suggesting a monarch determined to work through his illness rather than around it.

The figures, compiled by the Press Association from the Court Circular, capture the King crisscrossing the country: from the Eden Project in Cornwall to Grimsby Town Football Club, from Ards Allotments in County Down to a stretch of the newly expanded King Charles III England Coast Path in East Sussex. He took the controls of a tram-train near Cardiff, kicked off a game of hand ba’ in the Scottish Borders, and even stepped out of the Doctor Who Tardis at the Commonwealth Games opening ceremony in Glasgow.

View 3 Images The King has been keen to cement his legacy since his coronation in 2023 (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

Tuesday marks four years since the death of Queen Elizabeth II and the moment Charles became King. Despite being diagnosed with cancer early in his reign, palace officials insist the monarch has refused to let cancer define it.

Charles has also continued to shoulder the constitutional weight of the crown throughout his treatment. He held 26 formal audiences with his prime minister over the past year — 24 with Sir Keir Starmer and two with his successor Andy Burnham, who took over in July - and chaired 12 meetings of the Privy Council. He has kept up his diplomatic duties too, receiving Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky twice and, most recently, French President Emmanuel Macron in September.

The King’s stamina appears to have set the tone for the wider family. Queen Camilla, who accompanied her husband to both the US and the Vatican, carried out 114 days of engagements - more than in any of the previous three years of his reign. The Princess Royal remained the family’s hardest worker with 183 days, while the Duke of Edinburgh notched up 147, up from 130. The Prince and Princess of Wales also stepped up their workload, with William on 115 days and the princess on 63, both notable increases from the year before.

News.title: Gunman 'riding e-bike opens fire' on Bootle street as people run 'screaming'
News.content:
Gunman 'riding e-bike opens fire' on Bootle street as people run 'screaming'

People ran "screaming" on Stanley Road, in Bootle, Liverpool, after a witness told how a man riding an e-bike allegedly opened fire with a handgun with armed police scrambled

View 3 Images Police at the scene after a man reportedly opened fire in Bootle

A man reportedly opened fire on a busy street in Liverpool as people were heard “screaming”.

‌



Armed police were called to Stanley Road, at the junction with Balliol Road, shortly before 5pm today following reports a man riding an e-bike had fired shots from a handgun.

‌



A large cordon has now been put in place, with access restricted at its junctions with Merton Road and Balliol Road. There are currently no reports of injuries although Merseyside Police said there has been damage to property.

‌



Several police vehicles and officers were seen inside the cordon, while forensic teams later attended the scene and appeared to concentrate their work around the area of a bus stop.

View 3 Images Forensic officers gathering evidence in Bootle

A witness who was driving along Stanley Road at the time said they heard what sounded like two gunshots and told how a car around 20 meters ahead suddenly stop before reversing back towards them.

‌



They told the Liverpool Echo: “At that point, I didn’t know what was going on so I just waited behind for a second. What sounded like two gunshots were then fired. It was really loud; two bangs.

“Two people, I don’t know whether they were male or female, on big black bikes like e-bikes, whizzed off around the corner. About 20 seconds later, a guy came out of Swift’s pub holding a brick, with two other girls. He looked like he was looking for somebody.

“He and the girls were shouting. By this point, everyone had come out of the shops. People were everywhere, screaming on the street. I didn’t really know what was going on.”

‌



Armed officers remain in the area and detectives are carrying out CCTV and witness enquiries.

View 3 Images A police cordon is currently in place

Detective Chief Inspector Chris Saidi-Bidokhti said: “We are in the very early stages of an investigation and I would appeal to anyone who may have witnessed what happened or has any information which could help us with our enquiries to come forward.

‌



“I would also like to appeal to anyone who lives in the area, who has CCTV footage or Ring doorbell, that may have captured the incident to get in touch.

“We are relentless in our pursuit of such offenders who carry dangerous weapons in our community and urge anyone who has any information to contact us so we can find those responsible."

A statement from Merseyside Police read: "If you have any CCTV, dashcam or doorbell footage or information about this incident, please contact Merseyside Police social media desk via X @MerPolCC or on Facebook ‘Merseyside Police Contact Centre’.

Article continues below

"You can also report information via the force's website: https://www.merseyside.police.uk/ro/report/ocr/af/how-to-report-a-crime/ or call with log number 745 of 7 September. Alternatively, contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111, or via their website here: https://crimestoppers-uk.org/give-information/forms/give-information-anonymously In an emergency always call 999."

News.title: Turkey wildfire: Residents evacuated as flames spread towards homes in Antalya
News.content:
Turkey wildfire: Residents evacuated as flames spread towards homes in Antalya

Evacuations are underway around the Turkish tourist destination, Antalya, with hundreds of firefighters tackling wildfire which is spreading quickly through neighbourhoods

View 3 Images Evacuations are underway in Antalya, Turkey, with hundreds of firefighters tackling the blaze. (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

People have been evacuated as a wildfire rips through a tourist hotspot in Turkey, with flames spreading towards homes.

‌



The blaze is tearing through Antalya’s Aksu district after breaking out at around 6pm local time, with strong winds helping it spread into residential areas.

‌



One house has been completely destroyed, with smoke spreading from the Karaöz neighbourhood, according to Turkish outlet Cumhuriyet. The cause of the fire is unknown.

‌



Around 45 fire engines along with 275 firefighters are now trying to bring the forest fire under control along with the help of nine helicopters and three planes.

View 3 Images (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Many residents have been evacuated while the road running from Karaoz into the centre of Antalya has been closed to traffic due to flames.

‌



A statement from the Regional Forestry Directorate said: "Our teams are intervening from the air and the ground in the spot fires caused by flammable materials spreading due to the energy of the main fire."

Locals have also been trying to stop the progress of the wildfire by building barricades to protect their homes.

One resident Muhammet Özdemir told the media outlet Cumhuriyet: "They told me there was a fire near my house. Both the right and left sides are burning. It came right up to my house. There's nothing left, not even a tree."

‌



View 3 Images Evacuations are underway in Antalya, Turkey, with hundreds of firefighters tackling the blaze. (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Ahmet Karakış, an elected official for the Aksu district, confirmed that people had been evacuated with a house burnt down and fortunately there have not been any reported casualties.

He said: “We evacuated many houses in the neighbourhood immediately after the fire started. So far, one house has burned down completely. Thank God there are no casualties. We are working with all our might to extinguish the fire.”

Article continues below

The fire has spread in different directions due to the wind and has now reached the borders of the Döşemealtı, Kızıllı, and Ilıca districts with further evacuations taking place including at an animal shelter.

Police have told people to leave their homes as a precaution and water cannons are being deployed in the surrounding districts to stop the advancing wildfire while people have are not being allowed exit into the zone.

It comes after a summer where wildfires have ripped through large areas of Europe, including the UK, on an unprecedented scale due to extreme temperatures.

News.title: Boy, 11, dies after go-kart he was driving rolls into pond with girl, 8, onboard
News.content:
Boy, 11, dies after go-kart he was driving rolls into pond with girl, 8, onboard

A boy, aged 11, has died after the go-kart he was riding, with an eight-year-old girl also on board, rolled over into a pond in the town of Darien, Genesee County, in New York

View 2 Images Emergency services responded after a go-kart carrying two children rolled into a pond in Darien, New York (Image: Genesee County Sheriff’s Office)

An 11-year-old boy has died after the go-kart he was driving rolled into a pond with a young girl also on board, police say.

‌



Emergency services rushed to the incident in the town of Darien, Genesee County, in New York, where the boy is understood to have been driving the go-kart when it crashed into the water.

‌



The incident happened on Sunday afternoon with the boy reportedly trapped by the go-kart in the water with family and firefighters freeing him before he was given CPR at the scene.

‌



Genesee County Sheriff’s Office said police responded at around 2.30pm and the boy was taken by air ambulance to the Strong Memorial Hospital in Rochester but was pronounced dead on arrival.

View 2 Images The boy was taken by air ambulance to hospital but could not be saved (Image: Genesee County Sheriff’s Office)

‌

An 8-year-old girl passenger was treated at the scene added the Genesee County Sheriff’s Office. An investigation has been launched by police with no further information so far released, reported WIBV.

Many people have taken to social media to express their sadness at what happened and offer condolences.

One person wrote on Facebook: "So sad. I live on the same road. Saw the responders. Last I heard he was in serious condition, on his way to strong. My heart breaks for and goes out to that family."

Article continues below

A comment also read: "That’s so sad. Sending my prayer’s to their family and friend’s," and another stated: "I saw this call go out and really hoped it wasn’t a child I can’t imagine what this family is going through this is so sad."

While a further person added: "Prayers for the family and all involved in this this terrible tragedy."

News.title: 'Thousands mourning as 'Butcher of Bosnia' Ratko Mladic given hero's funeral should worry Europe'
News.content:
Europe should be worried by the scenes of thousands of people mourning and weeping for an unapologetic criminal who showed no sympathy for the genocide he led.

Ratko Mladic was the evil mastermind behind Europe's worst genocide since World War Two - the Srebrenica massacre. The infamous military leader capitalised on the fall of the unified Slavic nation of Yugoslavia to help wage a campaign of ethnic and religious cleansing that scars the Balkans to this day.

Mladic's father was a member of the Yugoslav Partisans, a communist-led anti-fascist resistance group to the Nazis in WW2 Yugoslavia. Nearly a decade on, the world today saw horror scenes of people rejoicing a son who rejected his father's fight to commit his own ethnically-charged genocide.

View 7 Images Crowds gathered as military members carried Mladic's coffin after a religious ceremony (Image: AP Photo/Darko Vojinovic)

‌



Mladic led the Bosnian Serb Army from 1992-1995 where he spearheaded his army to two of the most shocking and deadly war incidents of modern memory - the Srebrenica genocide and the Siege of Sarajevo. The general led the longest military siege of a capital city in modern history when his forces surrounded Sarajevo for 1,460 days and killed more than 11,000 people.

Innocent civilians were cut off from food and medicine while they lived their lives in terror from constant shelling and attacks from snipers, who attacked from the mountains surrounding the Bosnian capital. Decades on, the deadly siege has made its way to the courts in Italy where an investigation was opened last year into claims rich people travelled to Bosnia on "sniper safaris" to allegedly shoot and kill helpless civilians.

View 7 Images Around 11,000 people were killed during the Siege of Sarajevo (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

While the siege continues to be probed, the death of Mladic is the end of the second of three henchmen behind the horrors inflicted by the Serbian government and army in the 1990s. Slobodan Milosevic, Serbian president between 1989 and 1997, like Mladic was tried at the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia (ICTY) and imprisoned until his death in 2006.

‌



View 7 Images Mladic was dubbed the 'Butcher of Bosnia' (Image: AP Photo/Darko Vojinovic)

Radovan Karadzic, a psychiatrist turned president of the autonomous Bosnian Serb entity of Republika Srpska, was arrested in 2008 also convicted of genocide by the ICTY, in relation to his role in Srebrenica. Karadzic was also sentenced found guilty of crimes against humanity and war crimes by the ICTY. Karadzic, aged 81, is alive and still serving his sentence.

View 7 Images Ratko Mladic (L) with Radovan Karadzic (R) in 1993 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Unlike Karadzic and Milosevic, Mladic evaded justice for 16 years after the end of the horror war that shocked the world. He was protected by his family and elements of the security forces before he was eventually tracked down at his cousin's house in rural northern Serbia, in 2011.

‌



The tragic reality of Mladic's ethnic hatred will also be hidden from many for as long as the heroization of his character continues in scenes like those at his funeral. Parents in Serbia took their kids to church, on Monday, to pay their respects to a man who led the murder of more than 7,000 Muslim men and boys. Women and men cried as the 'Butcher of Bosnia' was given a hero's funeral.

View 7 Images Ratko Mladic was sentenced in 2017 for orchestrating the massacre in Srebrenica (Image: Getty Images)

They wept for the same man that stared at the families of his Srebrenica victims and drew a finger across his throat at the start of his trial. When Mladic was eventually sentenced he shouted: "This is all lies, you are all liars."

The Serbian government has refused to recognise that a genocide was committed in Srebrenica, calling the massacre a "horrific crime" instead. Today's worrying funeral scenes show how thousands are still gripped by a blind ultra-nationalism that fought against everything Mladic's own father stood for - Slav solidarity and anti-genocide.

‌



View 7 Images Bosnian women cry as their relatives who were killed in the Srebrenica massacre were buried, in 2005 (Image: AFP/GETTY IMAGES)

Mladic has even appeared to pull Serbia backwards even in death, with his funeral triggering a diplomatic spat between the nation and the European Union. Serbia is a candidate nation for EU membership but EU's foreign service said in a statement that "any glorification of war criminals, genocide denial and revisionism contradict the most fundamental European values and have no place in the EU or in EU candidate countries".

While the funeral arrangements were formally made by Mladic's family, the Serbian government sent a plane last week to bring his remains to Belgrade, and soldiers carried his coffin wrapped in the national flag.

The genocide general is still viewed as a hero by many Serbs. The mourning of the Serb chauvinist's life and positive memory of a recent bloody war between neighbours - that killed 100,000 people and saw over one million displaced - will leave the dream of a unified Europe in tatters.

News.title: Andy Burnham warns MPs must 'prevent politics of poison' spreading after Dover and Portsmouth protests
News.content:
Andy Burnham warns MPs must 'prevent politics of poison' spreading after Dover and Portsmouth protests

Hundreds of protestors dressed in black and wearing balaclavas descended on Dover and Portsmouth in protest at small boat crossings over the weekend

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has told Labour MPs they must "counter fear with positivity and hope" after violent anti-migrant protests erupted over the weekend (Image: AP Photo/Kirsty Wigglesworth)

Andy Burnham has told Labour MPs they must "counter fear with positivity and hope" after violent anti-migrant protests erupted over the weekend.

‌



In his first address to the Parliamentary Labour Party, the new Prime Minister told his colleagues there is "a lot at stake" and that they have "a solemn responsibility to prevent the politics of poison" spreading across Britain.

‌



Hundreds of protestors dressed in black and wearing balaclavas descended on Dover and Portsmouth in protest at small boat crossings over the weekend. The Government has condemned any "thuggish and intimidating" behaviour after scenes turned ugly, with several officers assaulted and police vehicles damaged.

‌



After referencing the protests, Mr Burnham said there was a need to focus on "positivity and hope". He told Labour MPs: “There's a lot at stake and it requires us to counter fear with positivity and hope. We have a responsibility in the times that we're living in.

"It's a solemn responsibility to prevent the politics of poison seeping into our streets. We are here to speak to the politics of hope and of positivity.”

Far-right Portsmouth protesters target RNLI heroes sparking backlash as police hunt masked thugs READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham said that for generations the Labour Party has had a proud record of bringing hope to people (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He added: "In the times in which we live, we've got to be quite clear and leave the public in no doubt about what Britain stands for. We stand for a sense of fairness, for justice. We will never, ever accept any form of racism in our communities."

Mr Burnham said that for generations the Labour Party has had a proud record of bringing hope to people. He continued: “We have to fulfil our historic mission all over again and bring hope to a divided country. To lift people and make them feel that things are possible. That we can make people's lives better. Make them feel that politics can work.

“We can give people a sense of positivity again. We can change this country for the better. Never accept the narrative that there's nothing we can do.”

‌



At the end of September, Mr Burnham will address his first Labour conference as party leader. Looking ahead, he told MPs: “At conference I will lay out in more detail what this phase of this Labour government is going to be about. One thing is for absolute certain: it's going to be about bringing back hope, bringing back hope in your community, in your constituency, and to the country.”

Mr Burnham took some 29 questions from Labour backbenchers in a packed committee room in Parliament. Cabinet ministers including Chancellor John Healey, First Secretary of State Lou Haigh and Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband were in attendance.

Elsewhere, the PM earlier held a phone call with Donald Trump, where the pair agreed on the need to work towards a ceasefire in Ukraine, as well as peace and security in the Middle East.

Article continues below

A Downing Street spokesman said: “On Ukraine, the two leaders agreed on the need to continue working towards a ceasefire that prevented more loss of life. The Prime Minister reiterated the UK's support for Ukraine and for recent US-led peace negotiations.

“On the Middle East, the Prime Minister set out the UK's commitment to working towards peace and security in the region, stressing the importance of the Two-State Solution, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and ensuring that Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon.

News.title: Far-right Portsmouth protesters target RNLI heroes sparking backlash as police hunt masked thugs
News.content:
'Thuggish' protestors faced an angry backlash today after they branded lifeboat heroes 'traitors' for rescuing a boat carrying asylum seekers in the Channel.

A far right group confronted the Royal National Lifeboat Institute crews on Sunday night in Portsmouth. The crews, who were based on the Isle of Wight, helped a 'mega dinghy' carrying around 120 people which was stranded in the Channel.

It came into UK waters from Cherbourg, near the ferry crossing for Portsmouth, rather than using the usual route from Calais into Dover, Kent. They were saved by lifeboat rescuers who returned to find a group of men in a boat shouting: “How do you feel bringing illegal migrants into this country?”

View 9 Images RNLI volunteers were targeted by far-right protesters in Portsmouth after helping rescue stranded migrants (Image: Barry Williams/PA Wire)

‌



A volunteer in a yellow life jacket told them: “I don’t know; I haven’t brought any in.” The protestors replied: "Look at these guys absolute traitors to this country. Look at the state of you.” Other footage posted also showed people shouting abuse at an RNLI crew on their boat. There were again calls of 'traitors' and 'Yellow jackets, yellowbellies'. A nother protestor described the lifesaving crews as 'scum'.

The RNLI defended their role, saying: "We are a voluntary lifesaving rescue service, tasked in the UK by HM Coastguard to assist anyone who is in trouble on the water. We will rescue those in danger without judgement or preference, as the RNLI has been doing for more than 200 years."

View 9 Images The RNLI has responded saying they will rescue people 'without judgement or preference' as the service has done for more than 200 years

Police have launched a hunt for the masked thugs who injured officers and damaged vehicles during the anti-migrant protests in Portsmouth. They are investigating potential assaults and criminal damage after black-clad activists attempted to block migrants being driven away overnight on Sunday.

‌



A small number of officers were injured and some vehicles damaged during the protest against the small boat crossings in Portsmouth. The man behind the balaclava protest in Dover on Saturday and the protest in Portsmouth on Sunday is said to be Danny Thomas, known as Danny Tommo. He became a close associate of the anti-migrant and anti-Muslim activist known as Tommy Robinson, real name Stephen Yaxley-Lennon. The government has condemned "intimidating and thuggish behaviour" in both protests.

View 9 Images Patriot Platform founder Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo speaking to Reform UK home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf in Portsmouth (Image: Pol Allingham/PA Wire)

People whose lives were saved by the lifeboat volunteers have since praised their actions and defended the RNLI. Marian Boyd, a Conservative councillor who is the mayor of North East Lincolnshire, is fund raising for the charity this year after her life was saved during a yacht race.

She told the Mirror: "From personal experience I was in a yachting race and caught in a storm when the RNLI came out to rescue us. So they are special to me because I was so anxious out there in the mouth of the Humber. It was freezing cold, and I have never been so glad to get back on dry land. We are up in North East Lincs, so the water is very deep and quite a few ships have gone down in the past.

‌



"At sea in a dinghy is very dangerous, you would not want to be out there in a under those circumstances. RNLI rescuers are unpaid. They get calls at all times of the day and night. I do not like the fact that there are so many boats coming over but I would not leave them out there to die."

View 9 Images Life boat jackets left at the scene in Portsmouth (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

She added: "There was a baby on board the other week, and my husband was saying, 'Why on earth would you bring a baby in on a boat like that?' But you cannot blame the RNLI. I remember when we went out, years ago now, it was a fine day with no storm forecast, it blew up without warning. That can happen at any time."

Writing on social media, one RNLI critic stated: “Do not donate to the RNLI. This scum organisation actively aids our traitorous Government in the invasion of this country.” But Andrew Douglas, 54, a boat tour operator who has worked for more than 30 years off the North East coast in Northumberland, described attacks on the RNLI as 'crazy'.

‌



He said: "You do not want people dying. It is their job and that is what they are there to do, the job that they do is fantastic. When it comes to somebody dying, you cannot just leave them. If they went into the sea with such low water temperatures, they would not last two minutes.

View 9 Images RNLI rescuers returned from helping the stranded migrants to find a group of men shouting abuse

"If there is a man drowning, you cannot ignore him because he is an immigrant. To slag off the RNLI for saving lives, it is not British. You cannot have something like that. I think it says something about modern life. Common sense and decency have gone out the window. When you are at sea all the time, you have the RNLI as a safety net. They make a massive difference and save so many lives."

Amanda Martin, Portsmouth North MP, praised the RNLI and emergency services. She added: "They deserve our thanks, support and respect, not threats and abuse. Everyone has the right to protest peacefully and make their views heard. But there is a very clear line between peaceful protest and disorder. RNLI crews are volunteers. They put their lives at risk to help people in danger. They are not political; they see someone in trouble at sea and help them, whatever their background. That is an important principle that must not be lost."

‌



In a Commons statement on the protests in Dover and Portsmouth, Policing minister Sarah Jones told MPs: “Peaceful protest is a fundamental part of our democracy and it must be defended. But so too is the right of other citizens to go about their lives without undue interference, and there can be no excuse for threatening behaviour or serious disruption.

View 9 Images Policing minister Sarah Jones made a statement in the Commons warning protesters who 'cross the line' into illegality will 'face the full force of the law' (Image: House of Commons/UK Parliament/PA Wire)

"Let me therefore make clear to the House and to the country that disorder of any kind will never be tolerated. And those who cross the line from peaceful protest into illegality will face the full force of the law. This government condemnds the intimidating and thuggish behaviour shown by some of the protesters this weekend."

She added that police in Kent and Hampshire have the Government’s “full backing” in taking “any necessary step to uphold public safety and maintain the peace”. Hampshire Police said that violence and criminal damage have no part in peaceful protest. “There is an investigation to identify offenders responsible for any assaults to officers, criminal damage to vehicles or other criminal offences has been launched,” they added.

‌



A National Police Chiefs’ Council spokesperson said: “Policing is committed to upholding and facilitating the right to lawful and peaceful protest, however we will not tolerate these rights being used to commit crime, particularly where that involves causing damage, disorder or serious disruption. Nationally, we have been supporting Kent Police and Hampshire & Isle of White Constabulary over the last few days in their response to recent events in their force areas.

View 9 Images Kent Police and the Hampshire & Isle of White Constabulary have been supported by the National Police Chiefs' Council (Image: Joe Sene/PA Wire)

“Mutual aid is routinely used to mobilise officers across the country to ensure public safety, which was utilised over the weekend. Policing continues to work with partners and the Home Office to develop its tools and tactics in response to serious disorder and has made significant improvements in recent years so policing can quickly and effectively deploy officers and teams around the country if needed.”

The stand-off came after crowds of masked, black-clad men blocked road access to the Port of Dover on Saturday, in scenes which have been condemned by politicians. Questions have been raised over whether police were adequately prepared. Nick Lowles, chief executive of Hope Not Hate, said there appeared to have been a failure of intelligence.

‌



He added: “To have 300, 400 people with balaclavas marching down the streets, stopping traffic. It’s not just good enough. We need to call these people out for their politics and for the type of Britain that they want to see. This is creating a climate of fear among migrants and immigrants, fear among people of colour. I think the government needs to be far more robust in standing up against this.”

The group behind the protests, Patriot Platform, was founded by far-right campaigner Daniel Thomas in July, and he has used social media to recruit supporters. The demonstration in Dover, Kent, brought traffic on routes to the UK’s busiest international ferry and passenger port to a halt, delaying some ferry services and blocking major roads.

View 9 Images Police in Portsmouth today in the aftermath of the protest at the rescue of immigrants on a boat from France (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

Kevin Moore, a former Det Chief Supt with Sussex Police, said: "People have got a right to protest but they should not be assaulting police officers or using fear of violence. There's legislation that says if you're going to have a demonstration you have to let the police know in advance."

‌



A grandfather said he had to deflate his own dinghy to stop protesters taking it on Sunday night. Barry John-Williams, 69, said the protesters were “idiots” and some had offered him money to use his boat. He added: “They were offering to pay me money to take the boat and I said: ‘Look it’s staying there,’ and that’s why I deflated it. What they were going to do with it, I don’t know."

“One of the idiots, I heard him say they thought the migrants might have come in this boat,” he added, referring to his own small 2.7 metre-long dinghy. The dinghy was met by RNLI lifeboats from the Isle of Wight when it reached UK waters, having set off from the Cherbourg area.

It is thought to have made one of the longest journeys of any small boat, and landings as far west as Hampshire are rare. Officials believe it was a one-off rather than new tactics. A Home Office spokesperson said: “We condemn the intimidating and thuggish behaviour we saw in Portsmouth last night. The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but it must never cross a line into disorder."

View 9 Images The protests have been branded 'thuggish' and 'intimidating' (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

‌



" This Government is doing the hard and necessary work of bearing down on small boats crossings, with the lowest number of June to August arrivals since 2020," the spokesperson added. Joe Robertson, Tory MP for the Isle of Wight East, writing to the Home Secretary, added: “I would like to take this opportunity to thank the brave lifeboat volunteers from Bembridge who were at sea for over 12 hours dealing with this very challenging situation.

"The RNLI is a charity established to save lives at sea and respond to boats in danger. It is not the job of the lifeboat to police UK waters. Anyone entering the UK without legal right to be here should be deported without delay by the Home Office, but when it comes to saving lives, every life matters no matter where you are from.”

It is not the first time RNLI rescuers have been targeted. In 2021, RNLI volunteers shared experiences of 'vile abuse' on the beach as they returned with people, including young children, in desperate need of medical attention, such as having beer cans thrown at them and people shouting “fuck off back to France”.

Richard Quigley, along with fellow Labour MPs from the Solent region, Satvir Kaur, Amanda Martin, Stephen Morgan, and Darren Paffey thanked rescuers, adding: "This Labour Government is cracking down on the evil, criminal smuggler gangs. Summer small boat crossings have fallen to a six-year low, and we are ending the use of asylum hotels for good. But we’re not complacent. We still have an enormous job ahead of us – but it’s one this government is going to tackle head on."

‌



The RNLI defended their crews, saying: "They handed the casualties to relevant authorities on reaching shore. Due to the large number of members of the public on scene, some of whom had entered the water, several of the lifeboats stayed afloat for some time as a precaution. Everyone at the RNLI remains focused on our core purpose of saving lives at sea."

News.title: UK government expected to announce restrictions on trade with West Bank settlements
News.content:
The UK government is to set out new restrictions on buying goods made in Jewish settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, the BBC understands.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is expected to outline the measures in the Commons on Tuesday, which could include restrictions on trade in agricultural products from settlements.

Last week, Miliband said he would unveil a "comprehensive reset" of the British government's policy on Israel.

The Israeli government has previously warned it would retaliate if any new measures were introduced.

Settlements are illegal under international law, and recent months have seen a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers.

One minister told the BBC: "The statement will be a complete reset of the nature of our Israel-Palestine relationship. It will all feel very different.

"It is not just about sanctions. We hope that this will finally achieve what those of us who have been working towards for two years over the Middle East have been working on."

BBC News has not seen the full details of the measures.

But Labour MPs who have been briefed on the plans believe the sanctions will target trade with illegal settlements. They believe that means the sanctions would cover both goods and services.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham confirmed to Labour MPs at their weekly parliamentary meeting on Monday night that Miliband would be making the statement, according to a number of MPs present.

The prime minister is also said to have told the meeting that he had briefed international leaders about plans in phone calls on Monday afternoon.

Burnham spoke to US President Donald Trump over the phone on Monday, during which the prime minister stressed the importance of a two-state solution in the Middle East.

An official account of the call released by No 10 did not specify that Burnham had briefed Trump on the sanctions, while the US - which is likely to strongly oppose the proposals - has not commented.

Speaking in July, Stephen Doughty - who was then Europe minister but has since been appointed Middle East minister - told the business select committee that existing powers to impose restrictions on settlements did not go far enough.

He said: "At the moment, we can sanction where there is evidence of it being linked to settler violence, but not, for example, in relation to a contractor working on the settlements. We need to expand our sanctions powers."

While ministers are said to recognise that banning a relatively small quantity of mostly agricultural products is a largely symbolic gesture, the government is expected to frame this announcement as a major reset in Britain's wider policy on Israel.

The expected announcement by the UK government comes after Israel opened up tenders for the construction of some 1,200 settlement homes in the so-called E1 area - a strategically important area east of Jerusalem. The plans have drawn widespread international condemnation.

Israel has held off on plans to build in the area for decades under global pressure.

News.title: Minister condemns disorder at Portsmouth anti-migrant protest after police officers hurt
News.content:
Council leader Steve Pitt said the decision had caused "needless disruption".

Around 200 people, some wearing masks, confronted police in riot gear after they descended on the Eastney Landing ferry port area, where the migrants were landed.

Police protected a number of coaches parked on a road leading away from Eastney Marina as protesters blocked traffic. A dispersal order was put in place, meaning anyone failing to comply with police could be arrested.

In a statement, Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said a handful of officers were treated at the scene for injuries, none of which were serious.

It said: "Violence and criminal damage have no part in peaceful protest.

"No arrests have been made at this time, however an investigation to identify offenders responsible for any assaults to officers, criminal damage to vehicles or other criminal offences has been launched."

Spencer Wragg, chair of Hampshire Police Federation, said: "I've seen footage of officers being pushed off their motorbikes, I've seen pictures of police vehicles damaged. It appears that the police last night became the target for some of the protest."

Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo - an associate of far-right activist Tommy Robinson - was livestreaming from the scene - where he called for his supporters to "get down to Eastney" and stop the migrants being transported.

The coaches carrying the migrants were able to leave in the early hours of Monday and the Border Force confirmed "individuals from the boat have been transported outside of Hampshire for processing".

News.title: King makes clear Harry and Meghan remain non-working royals
News.content:
The King's letter has been sent to Prince Harry's team, government departments, military officials and Lord Lieutenants, according to Palace sources.

Lord Lieutenants, who are the monarch's local representatives, and government staff are often involved in royal visits and engagements.

This letter makes clear that any engagements carried out by the Sussexes will be in a private capacity and they will not be representing the Royal Family.

It seems to be something of a shot across the bows, making clear that any Prince Harry and Meghan visits should not be treated as royal engagements.

This comes ahead of what are likely to be public appearances by the Sussexes this autumn, as they settle in the UK and support their charities.

The couple have kept a low profile, but the first picture of Prince Harry since coming back to the UK appears to have been posted on the social media account of Tower Bridge Studios in London.

The message from the King emphasises that the position agreed in 2020 when the Sussexes left the UK - the so-called Sandringham Agreement - is still in place.

This ruled out any "half-in and half-out" status, so Harry and Meghan could not pursue their own commercial interests while continuing to be working royals.

"It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of the Sovereign, and are no longer working members of the Royal Family," the letter says.

The letter sent on behalf of the King makes it clear that this remains the case.

"The charitable work of the Duke and Duchess is a personal matter for them both and undertaken in their private capacity," it adds.

The King's message says that any questions from organisations about the reception to be given to the Sussexes, "particularly where recourse to public funds may be required, should be directed to Buckingham Palace".

News.title: Faisal Islam: Chancellor's attempts to boost vibes may limit tax rises
News.content:
The chancellor may have thought about shifting the venue of his first major speech this morning.

It was an absolute and total coincidence that he chose to make it in the Coventry Manufacturing and Technology Centre (MTC), just a few minutes' drive from the city's totemic HQ of Jaguar Land Rover (JLR).

In the event, no one was pulling punches. The 4,000 office-based job losses at JLR were confirmed as John Healey answered questions a few miles away.

Healey chose to lean into it as an example of the global turbulence against which the UK needs more resilience.

The difference between this chancellor and his predecessor was he also feels that stressing fiscal discipline should instil confidence in consumers, businesses and investors, and not sap it away amid rolling fears of tax hikes.

So the prime minister and his chancellor have been engaged in a conscious attempt to boost the economic vibes - "a new story", as he called it.

In his speech, and in a BBC interview afterwards, this was clear. There are some positive underlying signs from consumer, business and recruiter confidence measures that indicate this message has been heard, although the hot weather and World Cup have also been factors.

The Downing Street duo are trying to maintain this precious commodity of confidence and the promotion of economic animal spirits that have been suppressed by years of political and economic chaos.

"Borrowing costs are too high," Healey acknowledged at the start of his speech. The global rise in bond yields is like a boa constrictor squeezing the Budget maths, slowly and relentlessly, occasionally loosening its grip, but never actually slithering away entirely.

It raises some reasonable questions therefore about how to balance reining in borrowing with protecting mildly better confidence?

The speech did not seem to me to prepare the ground - a "pitch roll" - for significant tax rises, as I heard at the equivalent Budget "scene setters" for the past two years.

"Am I right?" I asked the chancellor on this point. A pause as he sought precisely the right word formulation. "I won't comment. I can't comment. No chancellor can ahead of a Budget I will take and announce on October 28th".

OK, what about the advice from one of the PM's favourite economists Lord O'Neill that the rise in borrowing rates is a golden opportunity to scrap the triple lock?

This lock guarantees the state pension rising each year in line with either inflation, wage increases or 2.5% - whichever is the highest - but some have argued it is unaffordable.

"The prime minister has said, like I have, that we must bring down welfare costs, but we are also responding to the extreme pressure that is there in wider markets," Healey said.

Neither answer was a denial, but nor were they any type of confirmation. Like a stubborn batsman, the chancellor is going to stay at the crease, giving little away, in his case, about next month's Budget.

News.title: Self-described 'genocidal racist monster' jailed after BBC investigation
News.content:
"That bubble subsequently popped and he now has to take responsibility for those actions."

Sentencing Webster to two years, Judge Anthony Potter said he had been given numerous opportunities to show remorse and change his behaviour.

"Talk is very very cheap," he told Webster. "It has allowed you to escalate your offending and propagate the most harmful views.

"I cannot accept that there is a realistic prospect of rehabilitation in the community. I'd be failing in my public duty if I didn't send you to custody."

Frank Ferguson, the Chief Crown Prosecutor for the CPS, said inciting racial hatred was a "very serious offence" which went "beyond any debate about freedom of speech."

"Expressing a wish for people to be killedâ¦ Jewish people, Muslim people, black people, south-asian people, immigrants and LGBTQ+ community as wellâ¦ and encouraging other people to express similar views.

"It's not just about what he might do, it's what he might be encouraging others to do by his words," he said.

Det Ch Supt Alison Hurst, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing for the West Midlands, said Webster had been investigated previously for racially aggravated offences and thanked BBC Wales for bringing him to their attention again.

"Parts of the evidence from that documentary has been presented to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), which has led to the prosecution and sentencing," she said.

Webster was given a two-year sentence, where he'll serve half in prison and a year on licence.
