World.title: ECI announces bypolls to five Assembly seats, one Lok Sabha constituency on October 6
World.content:
The Election Commission on Monday (September 7, 2026) announced that bypolls to five Assembly constituencies in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry and one Lok Sabha seat in Assam would be held on October 6.

The nomination process will remain open until September 16, and counting will be held on October 9. The election process would be completed by October 11.

The by-elections were necessitated following the resignations of elected legislators across the three States and the Union Territory for various reasons. In Tamil Nadu, vacancies arose in Madurantakam (SC) and Dharapuram (SC) following the resignations of Maragatham Kumaravel and P. Sathyabama, respectively.

Ms. Kumaravel and Ms. Sathyabama both had been elected on AIADMK tickets in the 2026 Assembly polls and resigned after joining Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).

Five other Assembly seats in Tamil Nadu are vacant following resignations, including Tiruchirappalli East, which was won by the Chief Minister. He had won two seats and retained Perambur as his constituency. The other vacant seats—Ambasamudram, Karur, Veeralimalai and Perumdurai—have election petitions pending, preventing the EC from announcing bypolls there.

In Puducherry, the Thattanchavady constituency opened up after the resignation of N. Rangasamy. He had won from both Thattanchavady and Mangalam seats and decided to give up the former.

In West Bengal, Rejinagar and the high-profile Nandigram are up for election following the resignations of Humayun Kabir and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, respectively. Mr. Adhikari decided to retain the Bhabanipur seat where he had defeated incumbent Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.

Mr. Adhikari, who led the BJP to form its maiden government in West Bengal, had defeated Ms. Banerjee in her Bhabanipur stronghold by 15,105 votes. He had also defeated her in Nandigram in the 2021 Assembly polls.

Mr. Kabir, a former Trinamool Congress leader who floated the AJUP after his expulsion from the party, won from both Nowda and Rejinagar and decided to retain the former. He has offered the Rejinagar seat to Ms. Banerjee to contest.

It remains to be seen whether Ms. Banerjee will choose either Nandigram or Rejinagar to make a return to the Assembly.

In Assam, the bypoll will be held in the Nagaon Parliamentary Constituency following the resignation of Pradyut Bordoloi. He had won the constituency on a Congress ticket in 2024 and subsequently joined the BJP and won from Dispur in the recent Assembly polls.

Two other Lok Sabha seats—Shillong in Meghalaya and Basirhat in West Bengal—remain vacant, and polls have not been scheduled there yet.

Shillong fell vacant following the death of Voice of the People Party (VPP) MP Ricky Andrew J. Syngkon in February this year, while Basirhat has remained vacant since the death of Trinamool Congress MP Haji Sheikh Nurul Islam in September 2024.

The Model Code of Conduct will come into effect immediately in the respective districts encompassing the poll-bound constituencies, the ECI said in a statement.

While Electoral Photo Identity Cards (EPIC) remain the primary identification document, voters may present alternative approved documents, including passport, driving licence, PAN card, or official photo ID issued by government entities.

World.title: Are nicotine pouches beyond the law? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far:

A new study led by the ICMR-National Institute of Cancer Prevention and Research has found that nicotine pouches are reaching Indian cities through online platforms, hookah shops and gig delivery services. The study comes after a warning from the World Health Organization in May 2026 about the dangers these products pose. Yet it is far from settled which Indian law, if any, governs them.

What are nicotine pouches?

A nicotine pouch is a small, tobacco-free, tea-bag-like sack containing nicotine, flavorings, and plant-based fibers. Users tuck the pouch between their lip and gum for up to an hour, allowing nicotine to absorb directly into the bloodstream without smoke, vapour, or spitting. Unlike traditional smokeless tobacco like snuff or chewing tobacco, nicotine pouches do not contain tobacco leaf, dust, or stem. The nicotine used can be extracted from tobacco plants or created synthetically in a lab.

Are nicotine pouches regulated in the same manner as cigarettes and other tobacco products?

Marketing, advertising, and sales of cigarettes and other tobacco products are regulated by the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, 2003 and the rules (COTPA).

The definition of cigarettes and tobacco products is very specific and does not include “all products containing nicotine”. If the legislature intended to cover all substances containing nicotine, or “extracts of the tobacco plant”, it would have specifically said so. Restrictions on the freedom of trade and commerce must be strictly construed and since nicotine pouches are not among the products listed in the Cigarettes Act, they fall outside it.

Are these regulated by the Drugs Act?

Nicotine is not mentioned as a drug in any of the schedules of the Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 (Drugs Act). Nicotine patches and gums have, however, been approved as drugs by the Drug Controller General of India for therapeutic use in treating nicotine addiction. Schedule K under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 lists gums and lozenges and exempts them from licensing and prescription requirements if they contain less than 2 mg of nicotine.

If nicotine were not considered a drug at all, there would be no reason to exempt certain nicotine products in Schedule K. The very fact that only some nicotine products are exempted suggests that all others are meant to be regulated by the Drugs Act. A consequence of this is that a license is required to manufacture, import, distribute, or sell these products in India.

On the other hand, it seems reasonable that nicotine pouches are not like nicotine patches or gums that purport to treat nicotine addiction; they are a substitute for cigarettes and other tobacco products. They make no therapeutic claim and do not purport to treat addiction. They are therefore not drugs as defined in the Drugs Act.

Why are they not covered by the law banning vapes?

The import and sale of vapes have been specifically banned by the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019 (PECA). If vapes were drugs, there was no need for specific legislation to ban them; vape manufacturers and importers would require a license for both the liquid and the device from the DCGI, and the government could ban or regulate them under the Drugs Act or refuse to issue licenses even if they weren’t specifically banned. One could therefore infer from this that the government found it necessary to have a specific law to ban vapes because the Drugs Act did not grant it adequate power to ban them.

If the government did indeed intend to ban or regulate them in any manner, nicotine pouches would have been specifically mentioned, or as “other products containing nicotine” in the PECA, or other legislation. Since there is no specific legislation that bans nicotine pouches, is their import, manufacture, or sale freely permitted?

Could nicotine pouches be treated as food?

The Supreme Court relies on statutory definitions such as under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and the Food Safety and Standards Act defining food broadly to mean any processed, partially processed, or unprocessed substance intended for human consumption, including drink, chewing gum, and components used in preparation.

The court interprets food to cover any article used as food or drink for humans, including items that enter into the composition or preparation of human food. Landmark rulings, such as on supari or chewing tobacco products, establish that the definition has a very wide amplitude, encompassing items chewed or consumed. It would be possible to argue that nicotine pouches are actually food products, and not drugs, for the purposes of Indian law.

Can nicotine pouches be imported into India?

In India, import bans are controlled by two main laws: the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992 and the Customs Act, 1962. Together, these allow the government to restrict or completely block certain goods from entering the country.

The Foreign Trade Act, 1992 gives the Central government the power to prohibit, restrict, or regulate the import of goods. The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) manages this and publishes the official rules (ITC-HS classification) that specifically list which items are free, restricted, or completely banned.

Section 11 of the Customs Act, 1962 gives the government the power to issue notifications in the Official Gazette to completely or partially ban goods. The government can ban goods for many reasons, including: national security: protecting the country and public order; health and safety: protecting human, animal, or plant life; economic protection: saving foreign exchange or preventing injury to local businesses; environmental protection: conserving natural resources and preventing pollution; and law enforcement: preventing smuggling, counterfeit currency, or illegal drugs.

After the World Customs Organization updated the Harmonized System, a sub-category was introduced for oral nicotine products that do not involve combustion: 2404 91 30 covers tobacco-free single-use pouches of the Zyn or Lyft type, and 2404 91 90 covers other oral nicotine products not meant for therapeutic uses. This replaced the earlier classification: 2403 99 90 covered “other manufactured tobacco substitutes”, while 3004 40 90 / 2404 91 10 applied only to nicotine pouches or lozenges strictly classified as medicaments or smoking-cessation aids, such as nicotine chewing gum, lozenges or patches intended to help people quit smoking.

Under the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) schedule and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) rules, items with the IHS Code 2404 91 30 (Tobacco-free oral nicotine pouches) are categorised as “restricted”. This means that unlike “free” items, they cannot be cleared simply by paying duties. Unlike “prohibited” electronic cigarettes (e-cigarettes), they are not completely banned on paper, but they require a specific import license or permission from the DGFT.

How does the DGFT decide on granting a license to import?

The DGFT cross-references with health and other ministries. If the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) classifies recreational nicotine pouches as unapproved drugs, the DGFT will not issue an import license unless the importer possesses a valid pharma-grade No Objection Certificate (NOC) and manufacturing/import drug license. However, if nicotine pouches are considered as food, there should be no reason for an import license to be denied.

What about duty-free shops?

Nicotine pouches are currently available at a few duty-free stores at Indian airports. Such stores are licensed under Section 58 of the Customs Act and cannot claim to be entirely outside Indian law.

Nothing in the license issued under the Customs Act exempts them from the application of all other Indian laws.

Isn’t a duty free shop deemed to be outside the territory of India and it’s really the passengers who purchase from the shop who “imports” into India when they cross the customs control at the airport?

In the case of Flemingo Duty Free Shop Pvt. Ltd. v. Shri Kaushik Bhattacharya (2024), the Calcutta High Court was of the view that a duty-free store didn’t “import” goods into India because it was deemed to located outside India for the purposes of the Customs Act and as a result, the legal metrology act requiring goods sold there to be labelled in a particularly Indian manner wouldn’t apply.

That decision shouldn’t be read to support the view that no Indian law applies to duty-free shops. If no Indian law applied to duty-free shops, what happens if a murder occurred there or some group of passengers ransacked the shop? Could they claim that no crime has been committed because no Indian law applies to that space? Wouldn’t an Indian policeman have the power and duty to investigate and arrest the miscreants? Wouldn’t they be prosecuted in an Indian court?

They are exempt from the application of the Customs Act only in relation to payment to the Indian government of customs duties, levies and other taxes on the items that are sold.

What are the items that are permitted to be imported and sold in the duty free stores?

Duty free stores are also restricted in the items they can import and sell. Since only passengers entering or leaving the country can purchase items from these shops, they can only sell items that passengers are allowed to carry on the aircraft or into the country. These are listed in the Baggage Rules. If the duty free shop had no restrictions on what it could sell, could it sell narcotics, arms and ammunition, all kinds of opioids? Surely no country would allow that. That would be absurd.

Cigarettes, along with alcohol, jewellery, watches, food, and small electronic items, are specifically named in the list of items that are permitted to be sold in the duty free shops. Nicotine pouches aren’t specifically listed as items permitted to be sold in these shops. Given the specific classification under the Customs Act that categorises them as restricted, it is unlikely that a license has been issued for their import.

What is the legal position?

While it may seem that there are complex legal issues surrounding the import and sale of nicotine pouches, it really is quite a straightforward issue for the government to resolve; it will take no more than a few minutes for a notification to be issued under the Customs Act and the Foreign Trade Act banning, the import and sale of nicotine pouches in India on the basis of protecting health.

If the government moves as slowly as it did with vapes, pouches will become fashionable, and demand will settle in. A ban notified after that point will only produce smuggling on the scale we now see with vapes and cause damage to health that will be hard to mitigate.

(Murali Neelakantan is a lawyer)

World.title: BRS MLCs Tata Madhu, Naveen Kumar Reddy arrested over remarks against Speaker
World.content:
The Hyderabad police arrested BRS MLCs Tata Madhu and Naveen Kumar Reddy in connection with their alleged derogatory remarks against Telangana Legislative Assembly Speaker Gaddam Prasad Kumar, made amid the uproar that marked the Assembly proceedings on Monday (September 7, 2026).

The two MLCs were booked under the provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act following complaints over the remarks against the Speaker, who belongs to the Scheduled Caste community.

Mr. Madhu was arrested from the MLA quarters, while Mr. Naveen Kumar Reddy was taken into custody from his residence at Kokapet on Tuesday morning. Both were subsequently shifted to the Saifabad police station for further investigation.

The arrests come a day after the Assembly witnessed intense protests on the beahaviour of the BRS MLAs.

Mr Madhu allegedly made the derogatory remarks during a scuffle with the police when the BRS MLAS and the MLCs were prevented from entering into the Assembly for wearing black T-shirts with ‘objectionable’ content against the government.

The ruling Congress, BJP and the MIM strongly condemned the remarks, demanding action against those responsible. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Congress leaders had maintained that personal and derogatory attacks on the constitutional authority of the Speaker could not be allowed.

The developments also triggered a political confrontation between the Congress and BRS, with the Opposition alleging that the government was targeting its leaders, while the ruling party insisted that the law would take its course.

The police are questioning the two MLCs as part of the investigation and are examining the statements and other material related to the alleged remarks

World.title: 13 lakh Delhi voters deleted in pre-SIR mapping phase, highest in Phase-3 States
World.content:
Pooja Devi, 38, has been living at the same address in Kalkaji for the past two decades, employed in domestic work, raising her children, and regularly voting in elections. When the special intensive revision of electoral rolls began in the national capital in June, however, she did not get any enumeration form. Once the draft roll was published, she hoped to find her name in the list of those removed because they were absent, shifted, dead, or with duplicate names, known as the ASDD list, but her name was missing there too.

“My husband and children received their forms but I did not. I had also voted in the 2025 elections with them. My name is nowhere,” she said, flummoxed by the booth-level officer’s claim that no form was generated in her name.

Ms. Devi seems to be among the 13.39 lakh voters whose names were deleted from the electoral roll in Delhi this year, even before the SIR process started in June, according to The Hindu’s analysis of data available on the website of Delhi’s Chief Electoral Officer (CEO). The period from January to June was earmarked for ‘preparatory’ measures, including pre-SIR mapping by BLOs. Among the 17 States where the third phase of the SIR is now ongoing, Delhi is the only one to have seen this massive rate of deletion of names during the preparatory period itself.

Also Read | Delhi SIR: notices for over 33 lakh people to be issued only in English

Shrinking electorate

At the time of Assembly elections in February 2025, Delhi’s electorate stood at 1.56 crore voters. By June 16 this year, when the electoral roll was frozen before the SIR started, this had dropped to 1.45 crore, a decrease of 11.03 lakh names. A major chunk, 93%, of these names were removed during the five months of the pre-SIR mapping phase.

After the SIR started, a further 47.56 lakh names have been deleted in the draft roll published on August 31, meaning that so far, 37.6% or well over a third of the voters in the electoral roll during the 2025 Assembly election are no longer part of Delhi’s electorate.

Apart from the 13.39 lakh deletions since January, 1.65 lakh names were added to the roll during the five-month pre-SIR mapping period, while there were modifications in another 2.83 lakh voters’ names. This means that the net change between January and June 2026 was to shrink the electoral roll by 10.28 lakh names.

Also Read | Voter lists shrink by more than 15% since 2024 in States where SIR phase-3 draft lists are out

‘Continuous updation’

A senior official claimed this was a routine exercise. “This was part of the continous updation of rolls, for dead, duplicate and permanently shifted voters,” he said. However, he could not explain the large number of deletions.

For instance, in the entire period between February and December 2025, there were only 75,313 net deletions; over the next five months however, there were lakhs of deletions each month, peaking at 3.39 lakh names in April 2026 alone, according to The Hindu’s analysis of the ‘monthly polling summary of additions, deletions, and modifications’ available on the Delhi CEO website. Also, this list does not indicate the reason for deletion, whether absent, shifted, dead, or duplicates, unlike the list of names removed after the SIR enumeration phase.

Also Read | Delhi High Court rejects plea alleging exclusion of homeless from voter list due to SIR

‘Unprecedented’

Former Chief Election Commissioner of India S.Y. Quraishi termed the pre-SIR deletions in Delhi as “highly unusual” and “unprecedented”.

“This information should have come from the Election Commission itself. They should have issued a list of voter names removed, and explained the reasons for this scale of deletion. There should be no mystery or secrecy about this leading to investigations and speculations,” he told The Hindu.

Mr. Kumar and his office did not respond to The Hindu’s queries on the exercise, including whether notices were served to those whose names were deleted during the pre-SIR mapping exercise.

Also Read | Delhi SIR documents differ on categorisation of voters left out

Continuous updation rules

According to the Election Commission’s rules, continuous updation of the electoral roll happens through individual applications for new enrolments or objections, with BLO field verification required in cases of unregistered deaths and shifting of voters, only after receiving Form-7. In all such cases, a notice must be issued. The Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) can also take up deletions, corrections, or shifting of names suo motu, based on the BLO’s field report, with the stipulation that individual names must be displayed publicly before they are deleted.

There is no draft roll or claims and objections period for such routine updating exercises, unlike for special revisions. If more than 2% of electors are removed or where the same person objects to more than five cases, the ERO is required to personally verify the deletions to ensure accuracy, the EC rules say.

In the annual summary revision and the SIR, on the other hand, the existing roll is revised as a whole. A draft roll is published after door-to-door visits by the BLO, claims and objections are invited and processed, after which the revised final roll is published.

Pre-SIR mapping was carried out in Delhi to map the voters with the 2002 electoral roll to ease the burden on the BLOs during the SIR itself, and 43% of electors were mapped, as per information shared by Delhi CEO Ashok Kumar earlier. However, no information was shared on the deletions done.

Also Read | Delhi draft electoral roll out: How to check your name

Highest deletions in Delhi West

The pre-SIR deletions were much larger than in previous special summary revisions (SSR) in Delhi. The SSR undertaken just after the 2024 Lok Sabha election and before 2025 Assembly election, for instance, had seen only 1.41 lakh deletions, while the final roll saw a net increase in the size of the electorate, due to a higher number of new names added to the voter list.

During the continuous updation between February and December 2025, there were 75,313 deletions in total, woth several months in which no deletion requests were processed at all.

In 2026, however, there were lakhs of deletions each month across all constituencies, with the highest rate of deletions reported in April with 3.39 lakh, followed by May with 3 lakh. March followed with 2.5 lakh and February with 2 lakh.

Delhi West district reported the highest overall deletions of 2.32 lakh, followed by the North West (1.99 lakh), South West (1.40 lakh) and South East (1.39 lakh) districts. These are also the districts which saw the highest deletions during the SIR enumeration phase.

Other States that saw net reductions in their electorates between the 2024 Lok Sabha election and the beginning of the SIR were Uttarakhand (3.2 lakh), Arunachal Pradesh, Punjab, Odisha (2 lakh), and Chandigarh. Another 11 States reported net additions in their electorates.

World.title: Delhi building collapse death toll up to 7; HC orders citywide PG inspection, flags student housing woes
World.content:
The death toll in the collapse of a building housing students in the Satya Niketan area rose to seven on Monday, even as the Delhi High Court expressed deep concern over the safety of students living in similar paying guest (PG) accommodations across the national capital and directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to inspect all PG hostels under its jurisdiction within a week.

The Delhi Police arrested Hariram Gupta, 82, a retired Indian Air Force sergeant, his wife Urmila Gupta, 75, and their son Mahesh Gupta, 52. While the property was registered in Mrs. Gupta’s name, the men’s PG was allegedly being run by her husband and sun, police said. A search is ongoing for those operating the PG and the labour contractors that were carrying out repair work in the building’s basement. “Their role will also be examined in the case and accordingly action will be taken,” said Amit Goel, Deputy Commissioner of Police, South West.

Five officials of the MCD, the civic body responsible for issuing PG licenses and enforcing building norms, were suspended. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the government is exploring a policy to govern buildings used for several purposes, including PG accommodations.

Delhi building collapse: Follow LIVE updates on August 7, 2026

Shortage of hostels

In the High Court, a bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said the deaths raised serious concerns about the safety of students living in PG accommodations and the acute shortage of hostel facilities for outstation students in Delhi. The deceased students hailed from several States, including Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Madhya Pradesh.

The court directed the MCD to ascertain whether PG buildings in its jurisdiction had been constructed with valid permissions, whether they complied with building bye-laws, and whether any violations had taken place.

The High Court said the responsibility for the incident could not, prima facie, be confined to the property owner, as the role of university authorities and the MCD also required examination. It directed the civic body to conduct its inspection at the highest executive level and fix responsibility public servants if the collapsed building was found to have been constructed without authorisation.

Threat to students’ lives

“These PGs are not only very dangerous, they are causing threat to the lives, security to these students,” the Bench observed, stressing the need for greater hostel capacity for students coming to Delhi from across the country.

The court directed Delhi University to provide details of the number of such outstation students enrolled in its affiliated colleges and the number and capacity of hostels run by the university or the government. It questioned the absence of adequate hostel facilities, saying the shortage left students with little option but to depend on PGs and private hostels. The court also sought details of any statutory provisions governing PG accommodations in Delhi, while emphasising the need for a regulatory framework.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta assured the court that the State government was actively monitoring the situation and that no stone would be left unturned in the rescue operations.

The case will next be heard on September 25.

Three in critical condition

Over the course of the 28-hour rescue operation, at least 12 people were brought to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, while three were taken to Safdarjung hospital for treatment. At AIIMS, six people were brought dead, while one more person later succumbed to his injuries. At least three are said to be in a critical condition, the official statement from the hospital said. One person admitted is stable and receiving treatment, while another person was discharged on Sunday itself. The three patients at Safdarjung Hospital were also reported to be stable.

The rescue work was declared complete at 5 p.m. on Monday, with agencies saying the debris had been removed entirely from the site. The mortal remains of those deceased were handed over the family members, the police said.

World.title: e-KYC deadline for LPG users extended till Sept. 14
World.content:
The deadline for domestic cooking gas consumers to complete Aadhaar-based biometric authentication, or e-KYC, of their liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) connections has again been extended, this time to September 14.

Confirming the one-week extension, a senior official in one of the three oil marketing companies (OMCs) said about 88% of Telangana’s 1.26 crore LPG consumers have completed the process, ensuring continued access to refills at domestic rate.

For the remaining users, the rate at which cylinders will be supplied if they fail to complete e-KYC remains unclear, as the government is yet to take a decision. Repeated deadline extensions indicate that the focus remains on achieving maximum compliance with the e-KYC directive.

Sources in the oil industry, however, said the e-KYC initiative to ensure refills reach only those intended is unlikely to achieve 100% coverage. Many of those yet to comply are believed to be in possession of either multiple connections in their name or use connections registered in someone else’s name.

The pace of improvement in terms of the remaining consumers coming forward is slow, the official said. A week ago, the compliance level in the State stood at 86%. The deadline was extended several times in recent weeks, from August 23 to August 31 and then to September 7.

Meanwhile, in a separate development unrelated to the e-KYC exercise, the Union Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas on Monday advised the OMCs to reduce the 45 days waiting period for consumers in rural areas to book another refill to 25 days, bringing it in line with the norm prevailing in urban areas.

The gap, between two bookings, was introduced at the height of the West Asia crisis as a demand management measure. The revision follows current LPG supply position and considerable reduction in refill backlogs compared to the situation when the measure was introduced, the communication to the OMCs said.

World.title: Cheyyur, Gummidipoondi shortlisted for Chennai’s second airport
World.content:
In a significant development, the Tamil Nadu government has shortlisted two sites for Chennai's second airport and has asked the Airports Authority of India (AAI) to conduct a pre-feasibility study. The move comes nearly a week after Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced that the State government will drop the greenfield airport project planned at Parandur and will look for alternative sites.

Editorial | Grounded: On Tamil Nadu’s Parandur airport project

The Hindu was the first to report that two sites—Cheyyur and Gummidipoondi—are the top contenders for the project. It is now learnt that the State government has asked AAI to study Cheyyur in Chengalpattu district and Manellore, near Gummidipoondi, in Tiruvallur district. Sources said that a final decision will be taken after the AAI gives its recommendation in the pre-feasibility report.

A team from Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation (TIDCO) has already completed the first round of inspections for both the sites.

Sources said the Cheyyur site is about 40 km from the Puducherry airport and nearly 35 km from Kalpakkam. It is also nearly 100 km from the existing airport at Meenambakkam. The Manellore site is about 50 km from the city and 35 km from Sriharikota.

Sources said that even if AAI recommend one of the two sites, there could be some difficulty in getting the remaining approvals from various regulatory bodies, given the location of both sites. “While there is possibility for Cheyyur, provided the Ministry of Defence gives clearance, since the Indian Air Force, Tambaram, controls the airspace in the region. But Manellore in Gummidipoondi has some challenges,” a source said.

As the next step, a team of AAI officials will visit both sites and carry out an inspection, after which the report will be drafted. It is expected that AAI will submit the report in a few months. “The State government wants to start the process on the second airport soon. It will help if AAI speeds up and gives the report at the earliest,” another source said.

But another source pointed out that even if the State government wants to build the second airport soon, it may have to wait for a minimum of 5-7 years to make this project a reality.

World.title: Nepra clears key hurdle to competitive power market
World.content:
• Approves uniform charges for all Discos; participating bulk power consumers to pay Rs6.23-Rs19.62 per unit

• Clears path for first 400MW open-access electricity auction

ISLAMABAD: The Nat­ional Electric Power Regu­latory Authority (Nepra) on Monday approved use of system charges (UoSC) ranging from Rs6.23 to Rs19.62 per unit for bulk power consumers (BPCs) of all distribution companies participating in the competitive electricity trading market.

The approval paves the way for open-access consumers to participate in an upcoming 400-megawatt auction. The consumers will pay the fee to the national grid to transport electricity from the source to the user. The charge includes transmission and distribution costs, fixed grid charges and cross-subsidies.

Put together, a B-3 industrial consumer will be charged Rs6.23 per unit by the national grid, while a B-4 industrial consumer will pay Rs9.09 per unit. These charges will be in addition to the power supply rate, including generation costs, to be settled between private-sector power suppliers and BPCs. Currently, there are more than 3,000 BPCs across the country.

The UoSC for C-3 and C-2 single-point distribution consumers is set bet­ween Rs14.95 and Rs19.62 per unit. General supply consumers in the A-2 and A-3 categories will be charged Rs19.14 per unit.

Bulk power consumers who choose not to participate in the competitive wheeling auction will face significantly higher transport rates, ranging from Rs19.17 to Rs32.56 depending on their category. Non-participating B-3 and B-4 consumers will be charged Rs19.17 and Rs25.45 per unit, respectively. C-2 and C-3 consumers will pay Rs31.30 and Rs32.56, while A-2 and A-3 categories face a Rs32.08 charge.

A fixed grid charge of Rs1 per kilowatt per month, based on sanctioned load, will apply to all categories regardless of whether they participate in the competitive auction.

The uniform rate announcement for all distribution companies, incl­uding K-Electric, is aimed at formally launching the competitive wholesale elec­t­ricity market. Under the first phase, the Inde­pendent System Oper­ation (ISMO), a new power division entity, will auction 400MW of electricity within the next few months. The government has already allocated 800MW for auction in two phases.

Nepra issued the determination after reviewing submissions from the Power Division, ISMO, K-Electric and BPCs regarding the mechanism for determining and settling UoSC, including inter-Disco differentials, cross-subsidies and transmission and distribution (T&D) losses.

The Power Division had proposed that the impact of inter-DISCO differentials arising from uniform application of UoSC should not be imposed solely on wheeling consumers.

Nepra had earlier circulated a draft adjustment mechanism among relevant stakeholders for settling inter-Disco differentials. The regulator said the key principle was to ensure that UoSC applicable to open-access consumers remained equal to those applicable to similarly placed consumers of suppliers of last resort (SOLRs).

Based on the T&D losses of individual Discos, Nepra determined a uniform loss factor of 8.04 per cent at the 11kV level. For consumers connected at 132kV, the regulator approved a uniform loss factor of 1.51pc, as suggested by the Power Division.

Nepra ruled that the additional charge would apply to all consumers, inc­luding open-access consumers and SOLR consumers, to cover differences among distribution companies and K-Electric while maintaining uniformity.

The federal government had already appr­oved framework guidelines for the wheeling auction of 800MW of electricity through bilateral competitive trading and to move towards integrated energy planning across Pakistan.

Under the guidelines, 800MW of generation capacity will be sold through a competitive auction for five years. The volume will gradually increase after the initial trial phase, subject to government approval. Nepra was tasked with determining uniform wheeling and grid charges for bulk power consumers.

ISMO will now formally conduct an auction for 400MW under a process approved by Nepra a few days ago. The entity will announce the auction calendar and detailed procedures within days, without imposing an upper or lower limit on bid values, which will remain fixed for one year.

Under timelines set under the IMF programme, approval of the auction guidelines was targeted for December, while Nepra’s approval of uniform wheeling charges was scheduled for January 2026. Both deadlines have already been met.

Published in Dawn, September 8th, 2026

World.title: Legal challenge launched against PTI’s planned march on Islamabad
World.content:
• IHC CJ Dogar to take up petition against Sept 27 protest today

• Petitioner fears disruption of routine life, traffic, and businesses, seeks court intervention against use of provincial resources for march

• KP CM asks Karachi lawyers to join protest, says Imran not cutting any deals

ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has been moved against the PTI’s planned sit-in and nationwide protest scheduled for Sept 27, with the petitioner apprehending disruption of routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital.

IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar will hear the petition filed by citizen Waqas Ahmed on Tuesday.

The petitioner has made the inspectors general of police of all four provinces, Islamabad Police and Motorway Police, besides other relevant government authorities, as respondents. According to the petition, the PTI has announced a sit-in in Islamabad on Sept 27, which could cause inconvenience to citizens and commuters and adversely affect business activities in the capital.

The petitioner particularly raised concerns over the proposed participation of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, who, according to the PTI’s announcement, would lead the Islamabad-bound protest. The petition expressed apprehension that the resources and machinery of the provincial government could be utilised for political activity.

It sought directions to the provincial authorities not to involve themselves in any political activity and to confine themselves to their official responsibilities. The petitioner also sought appropriate directions to the respondents to ensure that the rights of ordinary citizens, commuters and business communities were not affected by the proposed protest. The petition came ahead of the PTI’s preparations for its Sept 27 mobilisation, which the party leadership declared would not remain confined to Islamabad.

CM invites lawyers

KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi spent the past few days in Sindh to mobilise the party supporters for the Sept 27 protest. Speaking at a convention organised by the Sindh High Court Bar Association on Monday, the CM, who reached Karachi despite hurdles, invited lawyers to participate in the PTI protest and maintained that his leader Imran Khan was standing firm for the future of the country and was not striking any deal for his release.

He said the Islamabad High Court had ordered his meeting with the party founder, while the Supreme Court had ordered hospitalisation of former premier, but that was to no avail. He added the judiciary was reluctant to timely fix the contempt applications for hearings.

The CM also complained about the obstacles on the route of his convoy. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari posted a welcome message on social media while his party’s government in Sindh placed obstacles in the way of his convoy and arrested the participants.

The CM apologised to the people of Sindh and Karachi for the inconvenience caused by his convoy’s movement. He, however, said the province already lacked adequate infrastructure and that even the available thoroughfares had been blocked.

Sept 27 protest

According to PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, the party’s call for Sept 27 is aimed at mobilising people across the country for the supremacy of the Constitution, rule of law, and release of PTI founder Imran Khan. He had clarified that demonstrations would be held in every city and district, maintaining that peaceful protest was a constitutional and legal right. “The people from every province and district would take to the streets as a nationwide, peaceful movement for their rights and the supremacy of the Constitution and law,” he had said.

Mr Raja had further said that the Sept 27 protest would be “Pakistan’s voice” and that the party would exercise what it considered its constitutional and legal right to hold peaceful demonstrations. He had also confirmed that KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi would lead the Sept 27 long march towards Islamabad, desc­ribing the planned mobilisation as a nationwide movement.

The preparations for the mobilisation have also seen the emergence of a volunteer organisation among PTI workers in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Last week, a group of ideological PTI workers announced the formation of a volunteer unit called ‘Pasdaran-i-Azm Imran Khan Pakistan’ to assist participants and provide support during the Sept 27 long march. The announcement was made by PTI leader Daniyal Khan Afridi, along with other party workers, at a press conference at the Peshawar Press Club.

Ishaq Tanoli in Karachi also contributed to this report

Published in Dawn, September 8th, 2026

World.title: Govt jacks up petrol price by Rs12.90, HSD by Rs3.72
World.content:
The government on Monday jacked up the price of petrol by Rs12.90 per litre while increasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.72 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs358.77 per litre while HSD will cost Rs381.77 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 8 (Tuesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Seven GB roads set for federal takeover to boost tourism
World.content:
• 464km of thoroughfares to be rehabilitated, maintained by NHA

• Federal cabinet to consider proposal after approval by GB cabinet

• Roads frequently damaged by landslides and flash floods

• Tour operators, hotel owners and transporters welcome PM’s initiatives

GILGIT: The federal government has identified seven roads spanning 464 kilometres across Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) for federalisation under Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s tourism initiative, with the routes to be constructed, widened, rehabilitated and maintained by the federal authorities to improve connectivity and promote tourism in the mountainous region.

An official of the National Highway Authority (NHA) told Dawn that Federal Communications Minister Abdul Aleem Khan had proposed to the GB government that seven key roads across the region be handed over to the Centre under PM’s tourism initiative. The seven roads identified include the 54km Astore-Chilim Chowki Road, 31km Deosai-Skardu Road, 100km Skardu-Khaplu Road, 17km Skardu (Thorgu)-Shigar Road and the 36km Karakoram Highway-Naltar to Satrangi Lake Road.

The remaining two routes, the 121km Thalichi-Astore-Rattu-Shounter Road and the 105km Gorikot-Shagarthang-Skardu Road, are currently under construction.

The NHA official said the proposal had been approved by the GB cabinet and a memorandum of understanding (MoU) had also been signed in this regard.

The move comes as the government seeks to expand tourism infrastructure in the region, where difficult terrain and limited road connectivity remain major challenges to exploiting its tourism potential.

The initiative is aimed at strengthening road connectivity to some of the region’s major tourism destinations, improving access to remote communities and facilitating travel across GB.

Roads in GB are frequently blocked by landslides, mudflows, heavy rainfall, avalanches, flash floods and glacial lake outburst floods (Glofs).

NHA’s role

Under the plan, the roads will be constructed, widened, rehabilitated and maintained by the NHA to improve connectivity and facilitate access to popular tourist destinations.

The official said that the proposal would be placed before the federal cabinet for approval. Once approved, the NHA would assume responsibility for the development and long-term upkeep of the seven road links, including their construction, widening, rehabilitation and maintenance.

Asked about funding, he said the federal government would provide funds for the project. Previously, the GB government had been bearing the cost of maintenance, widening and rehabilitation of the roads, he added.

The official said it had also been proposed that a toll tax be introduced for tourists visiting the scenic region, with a blanket exemption for local residents.

Revenue generated through the toll would be spent on improving the road network in GB, he said.

“With the number of tourists to Gilgit-Baltistan multiplying each year, the federal minister proposed introducing a toll tax to fund road infrastructure development. However, locals should be exempt from this tax,” the official said.

Move appreciated

People associated with the tourism sector, including hotel owners and transporters, welcomed the initiative and expressed hope that improved road maintenance and connectivity would help promote tourism.

Ikram Baig, president of the GB Association of Tour Operators, told Dawn that the initiative would help promote tourism in the region.

He said frequent road blockages were a serious issue for GB, as tourists were not only stranded for several days but residents also faced similar difficulties during bad weather.

He said there was hope for an improved road network in the region after the federal government assumed responsibility for the roads.

“This initiative can boost tourism. Delays in restoring road connectivity and frequent blockages have badly affected tourism in GB,” he said, adding that a reliable road network was essential for the sector.

Ayaz Ahmed Shigri, general secretary of the Alpine Club of Pakistan and owner of a guest house, said poor road connectivity remained a major hurdle to promoting tourism.

He too believed that the initiative would help enhance tourism in GB.

Asghar Khan, manager of Serena Hotel, told Dawn that tourists usually planned their visits according to fixed schedules.

He said frequent road blockages disrupted tourists’ plans and sometimes left them stranded in the region for days.

Such situations created a negative impression and discouraged tourists from visiting the region, he said.

“Many tourists, including national and international visitors, cancelled their plans to visit because of blocked roads,” Mr Khan said.

He said the federal government’s decision to take responsibility for the roads could help reduce the problem if the plan was implemented in its true spirit.

GB Tourism Minister Naiknaam Karim said accessibility played a major role in tourism development.

He said if the federal government took responsibility for the roads, the NHA could ensure better management and improvement of the network with greater resources.

Published in Dawn, September 8th, 2026

World.title: SC upholds Bait-ul-Mal aid for Hindu girls
World.content:
• Rejects plea against SHC order requiring Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal to pay Rs10,000 per month to each girl, with 10pc annual increase until marriage

• CJP says courts may look beyond legal questions to address underlying predicament

ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Monday rejected a plea filed by the Pakistan Bait-ul-Mal (PBM) challenging the Sindh High Court’s Dec 1, 2022, order directing the welfare institution to provide financial support to two Hindu minor girls.

A three-judge SC bench, headed by Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi and comprising Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Miangul Hassan Auran­gzeb, upheld the SHC Larkana Circuit Court’s order requiring the PBM to register the minors as beneficiaries for payment of monthly maintenance of Rs10,000 each, with an annual increase of 10 per cent, until their marriage.

Though the Supreme Court appreciated the concern shown by the high court for the welfare of the minors, it laid down a framework for future cases, stating that cases should be referred to the PBM for consideration where circumstances disclosed before a court appear to warrant recourse to the institution.

Bait-ul-Mal may thereafter facilitate the applicant by assessing their circumstances in accordance with the applicable policy and eligibility criteria and determining the extent of assistance.

“This course allows the concerned court to bring a deserving case within the reach of the welfare institution established to respond to it, without displacing the structure through which the PBM is required to administer its assistance,” the court observed.

The controversy stemmed from PBM’s challenge to the Dec 1, 2022, SHC order, which held that Ram Raj — the paternal grandfather of the two minor Hindu children — was not personally liable for their maintenance under the applicable family law. However, the high court also directed Bait-ul-Mal to register the minors as regular beneficiaries and pay each of them monthly maintenance.

It so happened that Shrimati Re­eta, a Hindu woman, married Ravi Kumar in 2012, and two minor daughters, Jasika and Sanika, were born of the marriage. Ravi Kumar later died by suicide on May 20, 2017.

With no independent source of income to maintain herself and her daughters after her husband’s death, Shrimati Reeta instituted proceedings before a family court in Jacobabad, seeking maintenance for the minors from one of the respondents, their paternal grandfather, Ram Raj.

Ram Raj’s own circumstances were scarcely better. Aged and infirm, he too lacked a source of income and a residence of his own and was living in a dharamshala (charitable shelter).

Nevertheless, the family court decreed the claim for maintenance and directed Ram Raj to pay Rs3,000 per month to each minor, with an annual increase of 10pc. The decree was maintained in appeal, after which Ram Raj invoked the constitutional jurisdiction of the SHC.

CJP Afridi observed in the judgement that courts were not infrequently faced with cases where resolution of the legal question at hand did not necessarily resolve the underlying predicament of the parties. Thus, in fully discharging its judicial function, a court may look beyond the immediate legal question and seek to address that predicament.

And when a state institution exists precisely for that purpose, the court may very well seek its assistance, he observed. The present case, the CJP noted, demonstrated precisely why such recourse may sometimes become necessary.

The judgement noted that the minors’ mother was a widow without an independent source of income, while their paternal grandfather, himself aged and infirm, was living in destitute conditions.

The judgement noted that the two children belonged to a religious minority in a country where minorities occupied a particularly vulnerable position, with social and economic hardships often bearing upon them with greater force.

While poverty, loss of familial support and other forms of hardship were difficult to withstand in themselves, their impact might be considerably more acute for those who already stood outside the social majority, the verdict said.

Therefore, institutions of the state must remain mindful of this reality, the judgement said, adding that for Jasika and Sanika, their minority status formed a crucial part of the wider context in which their need for support should be considered.

World.title: PTI warns against ‘hasty decisions’ on provinces
World.content:
• KP CM backs Sindh’s stance, says will not support new units without Imran’s nod

• Gohar says decision without consensus to weaken federation

• Senate opposition leader suggests collective stand against move

KARACHI: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday said the PTI would not back any move to create new provinces without the explicit approval of party founder Imran Khan, while PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan cautioned the federal government against “hasty decisions” that could weaken the federation.

Addressing a ceremony organised by the Sindh High Court Bar Association in Karachi, the KP chief minister said his party stood with the people of Sindh on the issue of provinces. He criticised the constitutional amendments, saying that out of 27 amendments so far made in the Constitution, people only benefited from the 18th and 25th amendments while other changes were allegedly aimed at giving exemption to those in power from accountability.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja claimed that changes to the country’s constitutional framework were being planned to introduce the 28th Constitutional Amendment that would alter the constitutional requirement of a two-thirds majority in a provincial assembly for the creation of provinces. “We opposed the 26th and 27th amendments and will oppose the 28th Amendment as well,” he maintained.

Gohar cautions against ‘hasty decisions’

PTI leader Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Monday cautioned against making any “hasty decision” regarding the creation of new provinces, saying it would weaken the federation. Speaking to reporters in the federal capital, the PTI chairman said that dividing any of the four provinces, if done against the will of their residents and their representatives, would “weaken the federation”.

“Let a consensus be formed first; a commission should be set up on it, and deliberations should be held. Eventually, the new parliament that will come, those public representatives should review and provide consensus,” the PTI chairman said.

He called for building consensus on the matter, similar to the large-scale political agreement reached at the time of the 18th Amendment in 2010.

“Any decision, if taken, should be made after that. Making any hasty decision, in our opinion, will be against the federation’s unity,” Mr Gohar said.

Senator notes lack of discussion

Opposition Leader in Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, who is part of the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), questioned the lack of a discussion in parliament on the matter.

During an interaction with journalists, the opposition leader said, “Neither the federal cabinet has made the decision, nor have the National Assembly or Senate or the provinces discussed it.”

“Why is this matter being raised when no discussion has been held? From whom is this [proposal]?” he asked.

The opposition leader contended that the PML-N’s “party policy was silent” on the matter. He suggested that the government should “gather all parties and take a collective stand against this dangerous move”. “The opposition would also support them for Constitutional supremacy and for Pakistan’s stability,” he added.

World.title: Sindh Assembly rejects demand for independent commission to probe HIV outbreak
World.content:
• Muttahida MPA’s resolution turned down by treasury benches

• Sharjeel slams federal ministers for launching campaign against 18th Amendment

• Calls upon Centre to end ‘discrimination’ in gas and electricity supply to Sindh

KARACHI: The Sindh Assembly on Monday rejected with majority votes an opposition resolution seeking constitution of an independent commission to probe the HIV/AIDS outbreak in the province.

Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan lawmaker Muhammad Aamir Siddiqui tabled a resolution in the house and expressed serious concern over the HIV outbreak in a Sindh Employees Social Security Institution (SESSI)-run hospitals.

According to his resolution: “This House expresses serious concern over the HIV-related issue reported at Valika Hospital and its possible impact on public health. This House recommends that the Government of Sindh constitute an independent commission to investigate the matter and determine whether HIV has spread beyond the reported cases and the extent of the issue across the province.

“The House further recommends that, until the completion of the inquiry, the concerned officers responsible for the matter be removed from their posts.”

Labour Minister Saeed Ghani opposed the resolution, saying work on the issue was already underway and an endowment fund had been established. He urged the mover to withdraw his resolution.

However, Mr Siddiqui preferred his resolution to be placed for a vote in the house, which rejected it with the majority votes of treasury members.

It may be noted that a couple of weeks ago the Sindh government had confirmed that over 100 children had been infected with HIV at Valika Hospital. It had set up a Rs2bn endowment fund for treatment and rehabilitation of affected children and their families.

Members’ absence irked speaker

The proceedings were hampered due to the absence of members, as neither the movers of five resolutions nor the lawmakers who had submitted questions were present in the house.

The session, chaired by Speaker Syed Owais Qadir Shah, could not take up most of the items on the agenda. With no mover present, all five resolutions scheduled for submission lapsed.

During Question Hour relating to the public health engineering department, no member was present to ask supplementary questions, following which the chair concluded it.

Expressing displeasure over the poor attendance, the speaker said that it had become a practice for members to submit questions and resolutions but remain absent when the business was taken up. “The minister has come prepared, but members are absent,” he remarked.

The speaker directed that members ensure their presence and stressed that seriousness was required for the effective functioning of the house.

The listed questions were submitted by the MQM-P members Muhammad Daniyal and Syed Muhammad Usman, who were not present in the house during Question Hour.

In reply to a private motion by MQM-P MPA Quratulain seeking installation of street lights on all highways, Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon said that all national highways fell under the jurisdiction of the federal government. He asked the member to raise the matter with her party’s representatives in the National Assembly.

Sharjeel slams federal ministers, defends 18th Amendment

Mr Memon then launched a detailed defence of the 18th Amendment, criticising recent statements by federal ministers including Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, Ahsan Iqbal, Khawaja Asif and Mustafa Kamal.

“Provinces have become autonomous after the 18th Amendment,” he said.

He accused the federal ministers of launching a regrettable campaign against to raise the matter with her party’s representatives in the National Assembly.

Sharjeel slams federal ministers, defends 18th Amendment

Mr Memon then launched a detailed defence of the 18th Amendment, criticising recent statements by federal ministers including Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, Ahsan Iqbal, Khawaja Asif and Mustafa Kamal.

“Provinces have become autonomous after the 18th Amendment,” he said.

He accused the federal ministers of launching a regrettable campaign against the 18th Amendment and demanded that the federation end what he termed discrimination in gas and electricity supply to the province.

The senior minister said that provinces had made significant gains in health, education and energy since the passage of the 18th Amendment, and critics in Islamabad should first review those results instead of questioning provincial autonomy.

“If Mustafa Kamal, Ahsan Iqbal, Khawaja Asif or any other federal minister has any objection to the 18th Amendment or the powers of the provinces, then they should come and speak in parliament,” he said, adding: “We have representatives in this assembly who are capable of answering every question constitutionally, legally and with statistics.”

Citing the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre and the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases as examples, the senior minister said that both institutions had transformed after devolution.

“NICVD is considered one of the best medical institutions in Pakistan. Thousands of people from across the country come there for free treatment. This is the result of this system and the powers given to the provinces,” he said.

Mr Memon said that more than 3,500 megawatts of electricity was being generated from Thar coal and fed into the national grid. “This electricity is not only for Sindh or any one city, but for the whole of Pakistan,” he said.

He further said universities and modern medical facilities had been established in cities like Sukkur, and that the provincial health department was now “standing on its own feet”.

The minister said that the residents were bearing the brunt of loadshedding despite the province’s contribution to the national grid.

Criticising power utilities for punishing people, he said: “If 20 people have not paid [their bills], take action against those 20. Where is the justice in punishing an entire village?”

Mr Memon said collective punishment violated basic constitutional principles. “An entire region cannot be punished because a few people have not paid their bills,” he said.

The senior minister also raised the issue of natural gas, saying Sindh had been producing large quantities for years but did not receive its due share.

He further questioned the disparity in infrastructure development, noting that Punjab’s motorway network had been built with federal funds.

He said that when motorways were built in Punjab, the credit was given to provincial government, although they were federal projects. “Sindh is also a part of this federation, so why is there discrimination against Sindh,” he asked.

The senior minister said that to date, a complete motorway network was not built across Sindh comparable to the one in Punjab.

Later, the house was adjourned to Tuesday (today).

World.title: ECC okays Rs6.6bn for bulletproof vehicles
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the Cabinet on Monday approved a supplementary grant of Rs6.6 billion to purchase 30 bulletproof vehicles for the upcoming Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit next year and allowed continuation of gas supply to two Punjab-based fertiliser plants.

The ECC meeting, presided over by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, was asked by the Cabinet Division to approve a supplementary grant of Rs12.6bn to purchase over 50 bulletproof vehicles for the movement of Heads of State during the SCO Summit. The Summit is to be hosted by Pakistan in September 2027.

The ECC discussed the proposal in detail and, after due deliberation, approved a Rs6.6bn grant for the purchase of 30 bullet-proof vehicles. It asked the Cabinet Division to revert later with any additional requirement, after conducting an in-depth need analysis for any further demand, and to bring up the case again if required.

The meeting considered a summary from the Ministry of National Food Security and Research (MoNFSR) on Minimum Indicative Prices for the tobacco crop and the revision of cess rates for 2026-27. However, the meeting was not satisfied with the justifications and concluded that the proposal required further justification. Accordingly, it deferred the agenda and directed the ministry to resubmit the proposal.

Extends gas supply to Fatima Fertiliser and Agritech amid LNG shortage

The meeting also approved the export of donkey meat and hides from the Gwadar Free Zone, along with the required safeguards, at the request of the MoNFSR and on the recommendations of the committee constituted to resolve issues relating to the matter.

The ECC also approved a request from the MoNFSR to continue the gas supply to Fatima Fertiliser and Agritech until Sept 30 under the existing arrangement, to ensure fertiliser production due to the non-availability of imported liquefied natural gas.

At the request of the Ministry of Federal Education & Professional Training, the ECC also approved a Rs5bn supplementary grant as seed money for the Daanish Schools Authority Fund, to be maintained under the Endowment framework.

In addition, the ECC conducted a progress review of the Pakistan Skills Impact Bond (PSIB) and set September 30, 2026, as the deadline for the Ministry of Federal Education & Professional Training to share substantive progress against the initiative, for which the GoP guarantee was extended.
