World.title: Consistency in illusions and inaction out of fear: barriers to Georgian-Abkhaz dialogue. An opinion from Tbilisi
World.content:
Georgian-Abkhaz dialogue

Numerous criticisms are heard regarding the foreign or domestic policy of the Georgian government. One of the main accusations is inattention and inaction toward the topic of conflicts. In an interview with conflict researcher Vano Abramashvili, we attempted to assess the reality in which peace policy finds itself today, to understand the reasons behind this reality, and, most importantly, to discuss future prospects.

Vano Abramashvili

Question: How would you evaluate the currently existing peace policy? Where are we now, and what processes are taking place on both the Georgian and Abkhaz sides?

Vano Abramashvili: Currently, we find ourselves in a paradigm-less peace. Georgian Dream has utilized “peace policy” in an entirely different sense. Issues regarding Georgian-Abkhaz relations are completely sidelined. As a result, the process has been left entirely to drift. There is also a total lack of trust toward this policy.

On the one hand, everyone realizes that the end of the war in Ukraine will have a major impact on what the situation will be in Abkhazia and the Tskhinvali region. It will also have a major impact on our policy. We have no guarantee whatsoever that this war will end favorably. Therefore, the Georgian side has entered a spiral of mistrust.

In domestic political discourse, the leading narrative is that we must fortify ourselves like a fortress, that we have no friends, and that everyone has their own interests. This approach has also affected the topic of conflicts.

Every policy and movement related to Abkhazia is perceived as a source of potential destabilization. The attitude is that no way out exists to resolve these problems. There is a feeling that even internal resources do not exist to take these steps.

It is a state of despair and hopelessness.

For our society, this is also an unfamiliar state, because today it seems there are not even alternative visions and ideas. Until now, there existed the idea of Euro-Atlantic integration and, against this backdrop, a vision for conducting peace policy. However, today this Western policy has been suspended. We do not even know how much time and what scale of work will be required of us to restore these damaged relations.

Added to all this is the altered geopolitical situation in the region and globally.

That is why I would call the current state a paradigm-less peace.

Question: Is this paradigm-less state artificially created, or does it simply reflect the reality that took shape after the August 2008 war?

Vano Abramashvili: I think that such a choice was made, and this reality did not create itself.

Any state, no matter what blow it receives, decides for itself what position to place itself in. Back then, the war ended with an undesirable outcome for Tbilisi. The idea of returning the regions through military force became unpopular, and conflict issues shifted entirely into the dimension of Russian-Georgian relations.

Georgian Dream inherited the peace policy of the United National Movement and, in its own way, tailored this policy to its own comfort. It is through this comfort based on nothing that we have arrived at today’s state.

Question: When describing this modern reality, the main attention and responsibility shift to the Georgian side. But if the conflict also has a second side—we must also evaluate the Abkhaz side and its steps. What is their approach and paradigm? What are they doing or not doing that serves to create this lack of perspective?

Vano Abramashvili: The main difference between the Georgian and Abkhaz sides is consistency. The Abkhaz know what they want. Whether it works out for them or not—that does not matter. Their consistent steps obey a logic.

On the Georgian side, it is not like that. Here, policies changed, and individuals changed.

Over the last thirty years, we have clearly seen who is consistent. We must also understand this issue correctly. You can be consistent even in your illusions. The Abkhaz do not have the resources and means to achieve their goals. Creating an independent state is impossible. It is a fact that they are trying to do this, although it is also clear that it is not working out for them.

The Russians also have a consistent vision and plan. There must be an alienation of Georgians and Abkhaz from one another, and Abkhazia must be turned into merely a territory. This territory will ultimately have no ethnic content or purpose.

When the Georgian political class does nothing on a large scale against this and refrains from taking potential political steps due to security risks and fears—this makes it easier for Russia to achieve this long-term goal.

Question: Peace policy must be mutual. Do you notice in Abkhaz political circles or civil society any kind of interest, change, or reflection regarding the policy they themselves carry out toward Georgia? Are there any signs visible that, given a desirable political environment and willingness, peace policy would become mutual?

Vano Abramashvili: A situational alliance with them is possible on many things. We say that peace policy requires two sides, but my argument is that currently not even one side exists.

Both sides today live our own lives; we are in parallel realities.

Let us take even the population of Gali, which is our and the Abkhazians’ natural point of intersection, and assess what special attention they feel from our side.

Neither side is actually interested in a positive peace policy. What we have is a negative peace. And this is merely the absence of war. Real peace requires clarifying where we are, what speaking positions we have, who is ready to concede what, and so forth.

Abkhaz society is even smaller than ours, and they have far fewer resources. Given the established political logic, it does not even surprise me that the first steps do not originate from there.

To evaluate peace steps, those steps must first exist. We cannot evaluate what simply does not exist. And this non-existence has its own understandable reasons.

Question: The architects of the current stagnation are the political forces on all three sides. If political will exists, what topics do you think are practical and future-oriented that would interest the Georgian and Abkhaz sides and “force” them to talk to each other?

Vano Abramashvili: These topics must relate to development – socio-economic and rights-based development, and the improvement of the standard of living.

Everything except status.

I think that even under the conditions of occupation with the Abkhaz, we can talk. It simply requires political will and the correct formats.

On our side, we do not see the ruling party demonstrating political courage, committing to a revolutionary change in a good sense, and taking any step.

Topics with which dialogue can be initiated and which are in the interest of both sides could be a shared living space. For example, energy, climate. Everyone wants to live in a predictable natural environment.

If we explicitly state that in the long-term perspective we aim for cohabitation in a unified state, it is important that democracy, as a political system and a political culture, exists on the ground. Accordingly, this too could be a matter of common touch.

“Georgian Dream” failed to draw the line between strengthening the de facto regime on the ground and protecting human rights, choosing instead to avoid touching this topic altogether in public policy. This, however, is a flawed approach.

Question: Considering the ongoing political processes, do you expect any kind of changes in the direction of peace policy? The war in Ukraine also breeds uncertainty. It is not clear where the processes are ultimately heading.

Vano Abramashvili: We see that conducting the war is costing Russia more and more. This cost is human, political, and economic as well. Accordingly, Russia should likely steer this conflict toward an end; it must end it in some form.

It is natural that the end of the war in Ukraine will exert a major influence on our region—whether it be a temporary freezing of the conflict, a pause, or its final end. But if political initiative is not demonstrated and a vision or formats for a renewed peace policy are not proposed, we may again fail to utilize this new geopolitical reality to strengthen the process of restoring trust.

In peace policy, the human dimension is important – how this policy translates into people’s lives. We are talking about living human beings, about the future. If our policy is not reflected in the lives of the people living there—first and foremost, the population of Gali – then it was never a real and sincere peace policy. It is more indicative of political messaging.

If you speak about poverty reduction, this requires concrete steps and instruments. Peace too is achieved and felt through concrete mechanisms at the human level: through security, social attention, and culture. When this is not present on the ground, a person cannot develop a feeling of peace merely through talks on television.

World.title: “Georgia against Ivanishvili!” – 38th Saturday march in Tbilisi | Video podcast “Protests in Georgia”
World.content:
Protests in Georgia against Ivanishvili

The traditional “Saturday march” in Tbilisi on September 5 was held under the main slogan “Georgia against Ivanishvili”. Speakers said democracy was declining in Georgia, relations with the EU and Western partners had sharply deteriorated, and the country’s EU integration process had been suspended despite Georgia already having candidate status.

Participants blamed the situation on Bidzina Ivanishvili, founder of the ruling Georgian Dream party and an oligarch widely seen as the country’s de facto ruler.

“Protests will continue until the Ivanishvili government leaves office,” march participants said.

The traditional Saturday march was held in Tbilisi for the 38th time. The demands remain unchanged: the release of detained protesters, new parliamentary elections and a return to the path of European integration.

For more than a year and half – since November 2024 – continuous protests have been taking place in Georgia, with demonstrators demanding that the country return to the path of European integration. The results of the parliamentary elections held in autumn 2024 are still not recognised by part of Georgian society. Every evening thousands, and often tens of thousands, gather in Tbilisi and several other cities. Over this time dozens of participants have been detained, many have faced criminal charges, and some have been sentenced to prison terms. For the first time in the history of independent Georgia, the country has up to 150 prisoners of conscience, including women. Among them is Mzia Amaglobeli, founder of the popular outlets Batumelebi and Netgazeti. In 2025 she was sentenced to two years in prison for slapping a police officer. Protesters demand the release of all political prisoners and the repeal of all anti-democratic laws adopted over the past two years. To suppress the protests, the ruling Georgian Dream party has increasingly tightened repression against civil society and the media. However, protests in various forms continue.

World.title: Uzbekistan's imports surge 17.8% to $29.6B in 7M2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 8. Uzbekistan’s imports reached $29.6 billion in the period from January through July 2026, increasing 17.8% year on year, as demand for machinery, industrial goods, chemicals and food products continued to drive the country’s import bill.

This was reflected in the report published by the National Statistics Committee of Uzbekistan.

According to the report, machinery and transport equipment remained the largest import category at $9.7 billion, accounting for 32.8% of total imports. Industrial goods followed at $4.4 billion, or 14.8%, while chemicals and related products totaled $3.6 billion, representing 12.1% of imports.

Food products and live animals amounted to $3.3 billion, with imports in this category increasing 41.9% year on year. Services imports reached $3.6 billion during the period.

Trend’s calculations show that machinery and transport equipment alone accounted for nearly one-third of Uzbekistan’s total import bill. The category also increased by about 20% compared with the same period last year, highlighting continued demand for equipment and transport assets.

Other categories also recorded notable increases. Imports of food products rose 41.9%, while chemicals increased 15.6%. Imports of miscellaneous manufactured goods reached $1.0 billion, up 14.0% year on year.

In Trend’s assessment, the structure of imports points to a combination of investment demand and growing domestic consumption. The dominant position of machinery and transport equipment suggests that a significant portion of external demand is linked to industrial modernization, infrastructure, and expansion of production capacity. At the same time, the rapid increase in food imports indicates stronger consumer demand and the need to supplement domestic supply.

The increase in imports is also contributing to Uzbekistan’s widening trade deficit. During January-July, exports amounted to $19.9 billion, meaning imports exceeded exports by approximately $9.7 billion.

Furthermore, Trend’s analysis shows that the pace and composition of import growth will be important for Uzbekistan’s external balance. Imports of machinery and industrial inputs can support future economic growth if they translate into higher domestic production and export capacity. However, continued rapid growth in consumption-related imports could place additional pressure on the trade balance.

Overall, Uzbekistan’s import growth remains broad-based, with capital and industrial goods making up the largest part of the import basket, while food imports are growing particularly quickly. The challenge for the economy will be to ensure that rising imports increasingly support productive investment and future export growth rather than widening external imbalances.

World.title: Kazakhstan’s resident deposits grow to new high in July 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 8. Resident deposits in Kazakhstan’s deposit-taking organizations increased by 1.5% in July 2026 to 50.9 trillion tenge ($111.8 billion), up 6% since the beginning of the year.

This was announced in a report published by the Agency of Kazakhstan for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market

According to the report, the growth was driven by an increase in deposits denominated in the national currency.

''Deposits of legal entities increased by 1.8% in July to 22.5 trillion tenge ($49.4 billion), while deposits of individuals rose by 1.3% to 28.4 trillion tenge ($62.4 billion). Tenge-denominated deposits increased by 2.3% month-on-month to 41.2 trillion tenge ($90.5 billion). Foreign-currency deposits decreased by 1.5% to 9.7 trillion tenge ($21.3 billion), partly due to the revaluation effect amid a 1.5% strengthening of the tenge against the US dollar,'' the report says.

As a result, the level of dollarization declined to 19.1% as of August 1, 2026, compared with 19.7% in June 2026.

The average interest rate on tenge-denominated term deposits of non-bank legal entities decreased to 15.9% in July from 16.2% in June. The rate on individual deposits remained unchanged at 14.7%.

Banks’ equity increased by 1.9% in July to 11.4 trillion tenge ($25.0 billion), driven by an increase in revaluation reserves. Since the beginning of 2026, banks’ equity has grown by 7.6%.

As of August 1, 2026, the capital adequacy ratio (k1) stood at 19.9%, while the equity adequacy ratio (k2) reached 20.7%, significantly exceeding the established regulatory requirements and providing a buffer against potential risks in the banking sector.

Since the beginning of 2026, Kazakhstan’s banks have recorded a net profit of 1.396 trillion tenge ($3.07 billion), down 14.9% compared with the same period of 2025.

Return on assets (ROA) stood at 3.5% as of August 1, compared with 3.7% as of July 1, while return on equity (ROE) decreased to 23.2% from 24.1%.

The figures were calculated using an exchange rate of $1 = 455.4 tenge.

The Agency's External Communications Department told Trend in an exclusive interview that it uses AI and machine learning technologies in its supervisory activities to improve the accuracy of financial institutions' risk assessments, accelerate analytical processes and automate data processing.

''The Agency uses artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in its supervisory activities to improve the accuracy of financial institutions' risk assessments, accelerate analytical processes, and automate data processing,'' the Agency said.

The press service noted that in 2025 the Agency approved its Digital Transformation Strategy for 2025–2027, which sets the priorities for digital development across its key areas of activity. According to the Agency, the strategy builds on previously implemented initiatives and marks the transition from introducing individual digital solutions to a comprehensive institutional transformation.

''As part of the Strategy's implementation, the first version of the unified supervisory platform, FinAI, was launched in 2025. The platform includes more than 20 supervisory tools, including 10 AI-powered services. It covers the entire supervisory cycle, from the registration of a financial institution to its liquidation, and includes licensing, prudential and conduct supervision, as well as anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing functions,'' the Agency said.

World.title: Counsellor at Azerbaijani Embassy in UK sends letter to The Guardian
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 8. The Guardian has published a response letter from Gunel Salimova, Counsellor at the Embassy of Azerbaijan in the United Kingdom, addressed to the newspaper’s editorial board in connection with a biased article.

The letter notes that, contrary to the author’s opinion, the aforementioned film The Black Garden contains a chauvinistic stance and does not reflect the existing reality.

It also stresses the importance of taking into account, when covering the former conflict, the tragedies experienced by the Azerbaijani people, the humanitarian and social consequences of the occupation, as well as the continuing threat posed by landmines. The letter also points out that the cause of the former conflict was Armenia’s occupation of Azerbaijani territories, and that Azerbaijan restored its territorial integrity in 2020.

It is emphasized that significant progress has been achieved towards establishing lasting peace between Azerbaijan and Armenia, and that the leaders of the two countries discussed concrete results of the peace process at their most recent meetings. In this regard, discussions on restoring trade ties between the two countries, the delimitation of borders, and regional connectivity projects are noted.

The Azerbaijani side is said to favor focusing attention not on the divisions arising from the former conflict, but on the positive results achieved towards strengthening peace, cooperation, and mutual trust in the region.

World.title: Lion turns down monster offer from rival, Saint demands trade
World.content:
Brisbane Lions premiership hero Zac Bailey has re-signed with the reigning premiers, ending a long-running saga about whether he would move to Adelaide.

In an added subplot to this Saturday night's semifinal between the Lions and the Crows at the Gabba, Bailey has turned down a monster offer from Adelaide.

The restricted free agent has penned a new eight-year deal to remain with the Lions until the end of 2034.

A two-time All-Australian, Bailey has enjoyed another outstanding season with 31 goals and averaged a career-high 21.7 disposals.

The 26-year-old's call comes as the Lions prepare to farewell star veteran Lachie Neale, who is expected to move to Collingwood during the trade period.

Bailey's signature comes just three days after the Lions were unexpectedly smashed by Sydney in the qualifying final at the SCG.

Marshall demands trade from Saints, Duursma wants to leave Roos

Meanwhile, Rowan Marshall is demanding a trade from St Kilda, a year after Geelong tried to lure the experienced ruckman.

Rowan Marshall wants to be traded away from St Kilda. (AAP: Morgan Hancock)

Marshall is contracted at the Saints until the end of next season, with the Cats and Essendon his strongest suitors.

He tried to leave for Geelong at the end of last season but has not yet nominated his preferred new club.

Cats coach Chris Scott was tight-lipped on his club's prospects of signing the 30-year-old.

"If I was [interested], I wouldn't tell you," Scott told reporters on Tuesday.

"It's an unfortunate situation. I think everyone would like us all to be a bit more open, but I think it's got to the stage now [where] the communication should be driven by the players themselves.

"I don't think it's our place to sort of speak on their behalf, so it's probably a question better directed at him."

Scott said the fact Marshall remained contracted at the Saints complicated matters.

Marshall played 21 games this season for the Saints, who opted for ex-Carlton recruit Tom de Koning as the club's first-choice ruck.

St Kilda said it would consider its options ahead of the trade period, which opens on October 5.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club," the statement said.

Meanwhile, the fourth pick from the 2023 draft, Zane Duursma, has told North Melbourne he wants to move to Melbourne.

Loading...

The Demons have long been linked to the 21-year-old, who has played 38 games for the Kangaroos in three seasons.

Duursma has resisted signing a fresh three-year contract offer from the Roos, who last week sacked veteran coach Alastair Clarkson.

The Demons are understood to have separately told former captain Jack Viney that he is welcome to explore a trade after an injury-cruelled season.

Viney, 32, played only one game — in Melbourne's wildcard finals loss to Carlton — after having pre-season Achilles surgery and then suffering back and toe injuries.

Viney, a premiership player in 2021, is contracted until the end of 2028.

AAP

World.title: Alan Jones's former colleague quizzed over 'loyalty' promise
World.content:
The trial of veteran broadcaster Alan Jones has heard a former colleague promised him "loyalty" and that he would "refute any lies" made by "lefties" after media stories emerged about Mr Jones's alleged offending.

A former 2GB colleague of Mr Jones is giving evidence in the NSW Local Court about allegations that Mr Jones kissed and touched a younger male colleague on multiple occasions at work and in the lift of his Circular Quay apartment in 2008.

Other witnesses have told the trial this former employee was at a Christmas lunch in 2008, saw Mr Jones rest his hand on the complainant's lap under the table and then later made a joke about him "copping a feel".

Alan Jones flanked by his lawyers Bryan Wrench and Chris Murphy. (ABC News: Ethan Rix)

Mr Jones has been charged with indecent assault of Complainant C at that lunch, one of 22 charges he has pleaded not guilty to.

But the witness, who the ABC will not name to protect the complainant's identity, has been accused by the crown of giving evidence to "assist" Mr Jones after denying any memory of attending the lunch.

Text messages revealed in court

Under cross-examination by the crown, the witness has been shown text messages he sent Mr Jones in 2023, when Sydney Morning Herald journalist Kate McClymont contacted him about reports of a 2GB staff member touching another staff member.

The witness agreed he forwarded Ms McClymont's enquiry to Mr Jones, and told him, "if you need me to refute any lies I of course will".

In the text exchange, the court heard the witness called Ms McClymont a "c***", a "low breed" and "pure evil".

Mr Jones replied: "I am sick of all this. [Ray] Hadley inspired."

Mr Hadley leaving court last week. (ABC News: Abubakr Sajid)

The witness agreed while he initially had no intention of returning Ms McClymont's enquiry, he then spoke with Mr Jones, who he recalls wanting him to talk to the journalist and tell her "the truth".

Crown prosecutor Georgina Wright SC put to the witness that he was trying to ingratiate himself with the defendant by sending offensive message about Ms McClymont.

"No, that's how I felt about her."

"You regard loyalty to [Mr Jones] as the upmost importance to your relationship with him, don't you?" Ms Wright asked.

The witness said he regarded loyalty as important in all of his friendships.

Witness accused of 'assisting' Jones

When Ms McClymont's first story about Mr Jones was published in 2023, the witness texted Mr Jones to say the allegations against the broadcaster were being made by "sick people" and that "everyone who loves you is right behind you".

Asked who he was calling "sick", the witness told the court he meant the "lefties that hate Mr Jones … there's a string of them".

Under repeated questioning about what he saw at the staff lunch, the witness denied memory of the event, or having ever seen Mr Jones behave inappropriately towards any staff member.

While another lunch guest said this witness did see the alleged assault, witness Jason Morrison also told the court he did not see it.

He also denied ever hearing any jokes about Mr Jones giving romantic attention to a younger colleague, or having made a joke about the complainant "copping a feel".

"I suggest you are sticking … to not recalling anything at all, to assist the defending in this trial, aren’t you?" Ms Wright asked. "Your lack of recollection is not genuine, is it?" "It is genuine, it was 18 years ago," the witness replied.

The trial continues.

World.title: Dutchman who knocked de Minaur out of US Open stages epic comeback
World.content:
Dutch tennis player Botic van de Zandschulp saved match point to avoid losing in straight sets, before staging a huge comeback to advance to the US Open quarterfinals.

The 30-year-old, who downed Australian Alex de Minaur in a second-round upset at Flushing Meadows, was on the brink of defeat against Frenchman Arthur Gea but recovered to make it to a grand slam quarterfinal for the second time in his career.

Gea, who got into the main draw tournament when 2022 runner-up Casper Ruud pulled out with a back injury, was trying to become the first lucky loser to make a men's singles grand slam quarterfinal.

After winning the opening two sets, Gea had match point in the third-set tiebreaker, but van de Zandschulp saved that, then staged his comeback to claim a 3-6, 6-7(0), 7-6(7), 7-6(3), 6-4 victory in 5 hours, 13 minutes.

It was the fourth-longest match in US Open history.

"I think this is probably better than the first quarterfinal I made here," van de Zandschulp said, referring to his other US Open quarterfinal appearance in 2021.

"It hasn't sunk in yet, but I think tomorrow it's going to be a great feeling."

Number 28 seed Alexander Blockx beat 24th seed Francisco Cerundolo 6-3, 4-6, 7-5, 7-5 to become the first man from Belgium to reach the US Open quarterfinals, where he will play Karen Khachanov.

Khachanov also needed five sets to advance to the quarterfinal stage, downing American 14th seed Learner Tien 7-5, 4-6, 6-7(6), 6-1, 6-4.

Men's number one seed Alexander Zverev is playing the final match of the day against Italian 21st seed Luciano Darderi.

ABC/AP

World.title: Border Force seizes 1.7m cigarettes, thousands of vapes in WA, NT raids
World.content:
The Australian Border Force (ABF) has seized more than a million illegal cigarettes and vapes in a series of raids throughout Western Australia and the Northern Territory in a joint operation with other federal, state and territory agencies.

In a statement today, an ABF spokesperson said Operation Tempest uncovered more than 1.7 million cigarettes and 504 kilograms of loose-leaf tobacco, along with more than 9,500 vapes and 6,310 oral nicotine pouches across 66 locations.

The spokesperson said the haul would have had a street value of more than $814,000 and represented almost $4 million in foregone taxes.

Law enforcement agencies raided 13 locations in Darwin and Katherine late last month, seizing more than 300kg of loose-leaf tobacco. (Supplied: ABF)

They said 66 people of interest were also identified during the six-day blitz late last month and authorities had applied for the closure of 15 shops as a result.

In the NT alone, the spokesperson said NT Health and Australian Taxation Office inspectors found more than 300,000 cigarettes, 306 kg of loose-leaf tobacco, more than 1,560 vapes and almost 3,000 oral nicotine pouches at 13 locations across Darwin and Katherine.

The sites included two car yards, a petrol station, eight shops, a postal depot and a residential property in Stuart Park, with the raids also turning up electronic devices, NSW number plates and drug paraphernalia.

The joint operation resulted in authorities applying for the closure of 15 shops in WA and the NT. (Supplied: ABF)

At the same time, WA Health officials searched 45 retail shops, while ABF officers in Perth, Mariginiup and Margaret River raided four storage facilities, two postal depots, a home and a shipping container stored on a rural property.

They seized more than 1.46 million cigarettes, 197 kg of loose-leaf tobacco and 7,900 vapes, along with 1,000 cigars, 3,360 oral nicotine pouches and 4 kg of MDMA, while agents screened passengers from 22 international flights for illicit tobacco.

It comes after the ABF allegedly discovered 433,400 cigarettes, 686 kg of loose-leaf tobacco and 50,200 single-use vapes inside a Darwin Storage unit in June.

ABF officers raided four storage facilities, two postal depots, a home and a shipping container in WA, finding more than a million cigarettes. (Supplied: ABF)

A month earlier, 103,600 illegally imported cigarettes and 39 kg of loose-leaf tobacco were also seized from an international mail carrier.

In a statement, ABF Commander Greg Dowse said criminals were working to "diversify" their activities "in an attempt to conceal their operations and maximise profits".

"No single agency can address illicit tobacco networks alone," he said.

The joint operation uncovered more than 9,500 vapes and 6,310 oral nicotine pouches across 66 locations. (Supplied: ABF)

"Success comes from coordinated action where intelligence, analytical capabilities, regulatory powers and enforcement actions are brought together to target the full criminal ecosystem, not just individual detections or actors."

Australian Federal Police Detective Acting Superintendent Pixie Fuhrmeister said the agency would continue to work with its law enforcement partners to "proactively target" and "disrupt" those involved.

The agents screened passengers from 22 international flights for illicit tobacco as part of Operation Tempest. (Supplied: ABF)

"The illicit tobacco trade is directly linked to acts of violence in our community and these crimes are executed by organised crime groups in their pursuit of power and profit," she said.

"Anyone who becomes involved in the illicit activity should be warned the AFP and its partners are committed to ongoing action to stop criminal enterprises profiting from everyday Australians."

As of today, authorities say there have been no arrests or charges laid in either jurisdiction.

World.title: Three paedophiles charged in first eight months of online sex offender register
World.content:
Three paedophiles have been charged with dozens of offences in the first eight months of Queensland's public child sex offender register.

The website, set up under Daniel's Law in honour of murdered Sunshine Coast teenager Daniel Morcombe, has had more than 400,000 visits since its launch in December.

It lists the photos and personal details of reportable offenders who fail to comply with their obligations or hide from police.

Residents can apply to view images of sex offenders in their local area, while parents and carers can apply to the police to find out if an adult having unsupervised contact with their child is a reportable offender.

The site launched on December 31, 2025.

Deputy Police Commissioner Cheryl Scanlon said three people had been charged with dozens of offences, including 68 counts for allegedly breaching their reporting obligations.

She said one person had also been charged with two counts of indecent treatment of a child under 12 and possession of child exploitation material.

"When you look at the opportunities for us out of that register and the work that's being done in such a short space of time, it is paying dividends," Deputy Commissioner Scanlon said.

New Qld public child sex offender register live The government says the new public child sex offender register is prepared for high traffic following its launch.

She said 19 reportable offenders had been identified as having unsupervised contact with a child following 231 applications submitted by parents and guardians.

In its first three months, the website had been visited more than 290,000 times and 38,800 locality applications were submitted.

In the first six months, the website had been visited more than 381,591 times, with 44,472 locality search applications submitted.

Now, after eight months, the website has been visited 405,330 times and 46,428 locality search applications have been submitted.

Premier David Crisafulli said it showed what happened when parents were given information and tools to keep their kids safe.

"This is about trying to shine a light on those monsters who try to lurk in the shadows, who try to run away from their past," he said.

"This is about making sure that if people don't uphold their end of the bargain, that they are able to be held accountable."

Daniel's parents Denise and Bruce Morcombe pictured with Dan Purdie and David Crisafulli at parliament last year. (ABC News: William Murray)

Daniel Morcombe's mother, Denise, said their foundation had been advocating for years for such a register.

"It is just one tool in the toolbox for parents to look after their children," she said.

Daniel's Law faced opposition when it was first introduced, including from the Queensland Council for for Civil Liberties, who said it may "create a false sense of security" as "most perpetrators of sex offences are known to their victims or their families".

The legislation introduced three new offences around prohibiting the misuse of information accessed or obtained from the public register, with penalties of up to 10 years' imprisonment.

In February, the first person to be charged over misusing the registry was given a six-month good behaviour bond, with the magistrate warning against "vigilantism".

World.title: Australia has a housing shortage but builders are still collapsing. Why?
World.content:
Across Australia, thousands of people are waiting to find out if their homes will be built, after several separate construction company collapses.

By far the biggest of those recent collapses has been the Bathla Group, a Sydney developer that's been one of Australia's largest affordable home builders.

Owing about $3.4 billion to private lenders, Bathla's voluntary administration has thrown the construction of more than 2,000 apartments into limbo, while jeopardising a further pipeline of 14,000 homes.

More builders going bust since COVID

Figures released last week show 3,472 Australian construction companies went bust in the financial year to June 30 2026: one in four (24.5 per cent) of all company insolvencies nationally.

The only good news? The number of builder insolvencies was slightly down for the first time since a steep rise began during COVID.

However, our research has found insolvencies in the construction sector remain consistently higher than in other industries. That makes it harder to build the housing we need.

Australia is falling further behind in meeting the federal government's 1.2 million new homes goal by 2029. Official forecasts released last month indicate the target won't be met until December 2030. New South Wales — Australia's largest housing market — may not meet its targets until March 2032, three years late on a five-year target.

There's no shortage of demand for new homes. What we lack is a construction system capable of delivering them reliably, sustainably and at scale.

Loading...

Bathla's financial ripple effects

On Monday, more than 200 of Bathla's 350 staff were stood down as the administrator continues to work on a rescue deal.

While most of its building projects are in Western Sydney, Bathla's collapse is being watched around Australia because of its wider financial impacts.

Like any company collapse, there are specific circumstances involved in Bathla's current woes. Its business model relied on high volumes of low-cost building.

The NSW building regulator has also conducted more than 40 inspections of Bathla sites in recent months, and ordered the builder to fix serious defects in one major development.

Bathla may have taken as many as 1,000 deposits from buyers for homes now stalled. But home buyers aren't the only people affected.

'Troubling developments' in private credit

As well as owing money to subcontractors, Bathla owes money to a long list of non‑bank lenders — also known as private credit firms.

This reflects the construction industry's heavy reliance on alternative finance, because banks have reduced their exposure to riskier lending.

On Friday, Australian Securities and Investments Commission chair Sarah Court said the corporate watchdog was closely following "several troubling developments in the private credit sector, most notably with the recent collapse of Bathla".

Court pointed out that many Australians are exposed to private credit through their superannuation funds — meaning "this is not some peripheral issue".

Owing about $3.4 billion to private lenders, Bathla's voluntary administration has thrown the construction of more than 2,000 apartments into limbo, while jeopardising a further pipeline of 14,000 homes. (ABC News: John Gunn)

The perfect storm hitting builders

Bathla is not an isolated case. The wider construction industry is under strain, with higher costs, thinner profit margins and rising risks.

Figures released last month show house construction costs are now 51 per cent higher than before COVID.

For builders with slim profit margins, the rise in costs can make some projects uneconomic.

With costs rising unpredictably, builders locked into fixed-price contracts are absorbing losses they cannot sustain. This was a major driver of the spike in builder insolvencies during COVID.

Falling house prices and poor market sentiment mean some projects no longer stack up financially.

Many investors and buyers are spooked by three interest rate rises this year, higher costs, and recent federal budget changes to housing tax concessions that have made housing less attractive to investors. The prospect of further interest rate increases is also likely to see projects stalled, as the market waits for conditions to improve.

Then there are ongoing shortages of tradespeople. On top of those, home builders are now competing with data centre builders for tradies, which has driven up salaries.

Little wonder construction insolvencies have risen back to pre-COVID levels, despite strong demand for housing.

Structural change is needed

Governments can't fix all the problems we face, such as price hikes driven by the Middle East war.

Bathla suspensions point to 'larger storm' Under voluntary administration and having stood down two-thirds its staff, embattled property developer Bathla Group leaves dozens of projects in limbo.

But federal, state and local governments are increasingly recognising their role in creating structural barriers to building more homes.

A Productivity Commission draft report released in July identified many of the problems we need to address, including restrictive land-use regulation, slow and inconsistent approvals, poor coordination on key infrastructure, and complex regulation. These all increase costs and delays.

Our 2025 report showed over-regulation is particularly hard on small builders, who struggle to comply with overlapping national, state and local requirements. That matters because our research also showed almost two-thirds (63 per cent) of building company collapses were concentrated among small builders.

The National Construction Code is another challenge. Even with some states deferring 2025 code changes, the national rules remain complex and frequently updated — again, making compliance difficult for small builders.

What's safer than houses?

Some builders are responding by pivoting to infrastructure and commercial projects, such as Victoria's Big Housing Build or Queensland's Olympics construction projects. These can offer more manageable terms and less exposure to market volatility.

Good builders can pick and choose their work. Right now, housing is the riskiest option on the table.

Until that changes, we're likely to see more Australian builders moving away from creating the homes we urgently need — along with more headlines about another builder going bust.

Lyndall Bryant is a senior lecturer and Amanda Bull is a lecturer at the Queensland University of Technology. This piece first appeared on The Conversation.

World.title: My 'friendship cupid' gave me connections I didn't think were possible
World.content:
I call my friend Isabel "friendship cupid".

To be clear, Isabel is not a cherub, and she doesn't carry a bow and arrow.

But she is a matchmaker of a different kind: the reason I have made several new and cherished friends.

It's been hard for me to make friends as an adult. My ever-present anxiety tells me it would be far safer to stay silent and isolated than to reach out and risk rejection.

I'm a wheelchair user and one of the few people still taking precautions against COVID, due to the impact these symptoms could have on my health. This means there are limited public spaces I can access safely and limited opportunities to meet new people in person.

That's why Isabel is so important to me.

She not only sees the opportunity for connection, but takes action to foster that connection.

When I don't believe in myself enough to reach out, she can be a friendship cupid for me.

Here's how it happened

Not long after Isabel and I became housemates, she encouraged me to message her sister, Matilda, because we have a lot in common.

Laura says encouragement has helped her forge lasting friendships. (Supplied: Laura Pettenuzzo)

I took a few months to reach out, because even with Isabel's prompting, I was anxious, perhaps even more than I would have been without it.

What if Matilda and I didn't get along? What would I tell Isabel? Would I have failed some implicit test if Matilda didn't like me?

I didn't need to worry. Matilda and I clicked instantly, our conversation flowing naturally.

With Matilda, three hours often feels like five minutes, and there's still so much more we could say to one another.

We live several hours apart and don't see each other in person often, but I'm always enlivened when we do.

Isabel's matchmaking was spot on, and she is far from the only friendship cupid I've been lucky enough to encounter.

One of my former co-workers told me repeatedly how similar I was to her friend Nic, how our lives had so many parallels. When she started a group chat with the three of us, and invited Nic and I to a group video call, I saw immediately that she was right.

Laura (second from left) with three friends, including Shirley (left) and Kate (second from right). (Supplied: Laura Petenuzzo)

Nic and I have been friends for almost five years now and in that time she's supported stuck by me through good times and bad. She's celebrated my achievements and stuck by me as I've made many mistakes.

When I've struggled with my mental health, I've hurt her and pushed her away. But she's been gracious enough to listen to me apologise and take accountability. She has forgiven me.

I'm attending her wedding at the end of this year, all thanks to that one video chat.

Nic and I are also a great example of the success of friendship cupids creating friendship groups.

As well as introducing me to her sister, Isabel also introduced me to her best friend, Nicola. Matilda, Nicola and I have a group chat, and I have a photo of the three of us stuck to my fridge. Fittingly, I met Isabel through another friend, our bond another match well made.

I hope that one day, I can continue the friendship chain, can pay it forward and be a friendship cupid for someone else.

The lasting impact

While this whole process sounds a little like networking, I prefer to think of it as something much more than that.

My friendship cupid cared enough to build connections between others, without expecting anything in return. Without expecting these connections to last the distance.

Even though rejection from a potential friend might hurt, it doesn't mean I stop trying (I might just hibernate for a few days to pull myself back together).

The beauty I've discovered is in my willingness to be open to connection, and to facilitate that connection for other people.

Not everyone has that willingness, but I've found that some people — my people — do, and our lives are better for it.

World.title: Why a far-right party's victory in Germany is a 'serious moment in Europe'
World.content:
Europe has witnessed a steady series of incursions from the far-right of politics in recent years, from Austria and Hungary to France, the UK and Italy.

From an Australian perspective, these incursions seem to reflect the same trends we see in Australia with the resurgence of One Nation: a populist far-right party, trading particularly on anti-immigration sentiment and long-running simmering resentment over stalling living standards.

But the weekend win by Germany's AfD (Alternative for Germany) party in the state of Saxony-Anhalt has sent particular shivers across the continent and points to a political landscape that is much darker than the one being promised by One Nation.

The weekend win is troubling because Germany has been so particularly sensitive to the rise of the far-right in the past, and has tried to guard against it, because of its history.

Ulrich Siegmund, whose face is seen on the sign, was AfD's top candidate in Saxony-Anhalt. (Reuters: Thilo Schmuelgen)

The AfD wants to stop the teaching of Germany's Nazi past and see school classes focus instead on the glory days of Prussia, the Napoleonic wars, German unification, the "Iron Chancellor" Otto von Bismarck and the founding of the German Empire in 1871.

The party's branch in Saxony-Anhalt has been designated a "right wing extremist organisation" by the state's domestic intelligence service (which the party says it will abolish if it wins government).

That is not just because of what it called the party's "numerous Islamophobic, racist, and even anti-Semitic statements".

It is because it says the AfD aims to "abolish parliamentary democracy in its current form" and "continually strives to denigrate the democratic system of the Federal Republic of Germany, its institutions, and their representatives in order to fundamentally erode public trust in them".

Behind the rise of Germany's far right Far-right party Alternative for Germany is running second in national polls. Here's how it got there.

The intelligence agency notes there have already been open calls within the AfD in the state "for a military coup against the German government".

Many of its policies, particularly its anti-immigrant stance, are echoes of those of other far-right parties across Europe.

But what is most alarming to other countries in western Europe is a central pledge of the AfD, which has a particularly strong support base in the old East German states, to pursue a rapprochement with Russia.

It wants to expand Russian-language instruction in schools, end sanctions against Russia imposed since the Ukraine war began in 2022, reject and even expel Ukrainian refugees, and cut support for Ukraine in its war with Russia.

Germany has been the largest bilateral supporter of Ukraine in Europe, not just providing billions of euros in financial support but also being a crucial conduit of weapons as the US has withdrawn from supplying them.

If the AfD's win on the weekend was to put pressure on the national government's pro-Ukrainian policies under current Chancellor Friedrich Merz, it could decisively change the balance of the war.

AfD's state win can have national impact

In a leaf out of Donald Trump's playbook, the party has promised mass deportations of migrants as well as more detention pending deportation, mandatory work for asylum-seekers, and a cut to all state funding for integration programs.

Children who do not have permanent residency in Germany would be stopped from attending regular schools, as would children with disabilities.

A proposal to allow "citizens watch" groups, essentially police auxiliary forces, to help crack down on "left wing extremism" has sent a particular chill through those who remember Germany's past.

The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party has had a victory in state elections, prompting protests in Berlin. (Reuters: Maryam Majd)

They say the groups would be tantamount to vigilantes let loose in a legal system that would be reformed to allow more freedom of expression by limiting the enforcement of "so-called hate crimes" and cutting funding to pro-democracy education campaigns.

The AfD wants to change the school curriculum to stop the "perpetuation of a guilt complex" by educating children about the country's Nazi past.

Schools would also be banned from flying rainbow flags, as part of a general move against LGBTQ+ communities, but would be required to fly national flags and sing the national anthem.

It wants to boost the birthrate by introducing "welcome money" for couples who have children, reducing childcare costs, and offering free school meals.

The party itself is quite open about the fact it has seen this state election as the springboard to national power at the 2029 elections in the largest economy in Europe.

Its campaign slogan was "It starts here", and the party is leading the national polls with 28 per cent of the vote, compared to the CDU — Merz's Christian Democratic-based centrist party which has dominated post-war German politics — on 20 per cent.

Ulrich Siegmund says the party has "made history". (Reuters: Liesa Johannssen)

Even without any further parliamentary wins, its influence will be felt in the national parliament, the Bundestag, because the states have representation in the upper house, the Bundesrat, where the AfD can exert influence on policy areas on which it has particularly campaigned in the state election: education, culture and domestic security.

There is also anxiety about the security implications of a party with ties to Russia gaining access to intelligence briefs.

Many of the AfD's policies are not ones directly in the control of state governments. For example, it has been campaigning against climate change policies and the Paris climate agreement. But specifically in the very rural Saxony-Anhalt, it has been campaigning against wind turbines.

And the irony of its anti-immigrant policy is that Saxony-Anhalt has faced a major decline in its population since reunification in 1990. The many people who have left to find work elsewhere have left it with the oldest and most sharply declining population in the country.

It is therefore dependent on migrant workers to fill jobs in areas like healthcare.

AfD victory a 'serious moment in Europe'

The states do have some say over cultural policy. The AfD's targets include cutting funding from public broadcasters, which it argues are rife with "leftwing propaganda lackeys", as well as rejecting Bauhaus architecture, which had its roots in Saxony-Anhalt, as "too globalist".

"We have made history in this country," said Ulrich Siegmund, the party's 35-year-old leader in Saxony-Anhalt.

The win, and a staggering loss of support for Merz's party, have led to widespread speculation that the CDU may crumble internally as MPs from the old Eastern states either desert it for the AfD or pressure Berlin to change course.

The AfD's state election win has sparked protests in Berlin. (Reuters: Maryam Majd)

The AfD is also hostile to NATO, and the EU.

The AfD's win was welcomed by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who praised a "historic win for the pragmatic AfD", as well as by Donald Trump and Elon Musk.

But France's Europe minister, Benjamin Haddad, described the win as "a serious moment in Europe", warning that "nationalism and xenophobia will never be a solution".

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that "in Poland, only idiots or traitors can rejoice at the triumph of the AfD in Germany".

Until now, the rise of the AfD has been largely a phenomenon confined to the old East.

There is a strange mix of nostalgia for the days of state supply of services and a blurred memory of the repression which accompanied the old regime, as well as a possible greater tolerance for authoritarian leaders that has not been displaced by the experience of democracy.

Loading

Ulrich Siegmund, the party's state leader, told the Financial Times that his parents' experience of communist propaganda and pervasive Stasi surveillance taught him to question authority from an early age.

"That is somehow culturally ingrained here," he says. "People simply won't let themselves be taken for a ride."

But the AfD is now leading national polls and has gained significant support in the old West too.

Not everything has been going the far-right's way in Europe recently.

Notably, we witnessed the downfall of Viktor Orbán in Hungary in April, replaced by the centre-right government of Péter Magyar, who has quickly moved to dismantle pro-Orban state media and reform the courts and constitution.

Italy's 'fierce' PM is facing another huge test Giorgia Meloni is now Italy's longest-serving prime minister since World War II, but a big challenge is coming from the country's far right.

The right's Giorgia Meloni, who has just become the longest serving prime minister in Italy since World War II, has significantly moderated her positions to much more pragmatic ones since coming to office.

She has taken a more pro-European position, as well as firmed up her support for Ukraine and NATO, even though she has continued to support conservative identity politics and strict controls on migration.

But if the AfD is able to form government in Saxony-Anhalt — it is still a few seats short — and then secure wins in state elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania later this month, it could embolden the right across Europe.

As we have seen in Trump's America, an unleashed political force prepared to break all the rules and that finds itself politically rewarded rather than punished, only becomes bolder.

World.title: The two WA regions where the world’s AI companies want to build data centres
World.content:
NationalWAData centres The two WA regions where the world’s AI companies want to build data centres Hamish Hastie September 8, 2026 — 1:35pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

AI companies and data centre builders have approached the WA government with proposals to build data centres in WA’s Mid West and North West regions, Premier Roger Cook has confirmed. Speaking at a Committee for the Economic Development of Australia breakfast in Perth on Tuesday morning, Cook made the revelation when asked about the opportunities for data centres to be built in the state. Companies have expressed interest in building data centre’s in WA’s regional areas. Getty “We’re getting a lot of proposals at the moment from data centre developers looking to develop in less populated areas such as the Mid West and the North West, because they still maintain that connection, that connectivity, but are less impugned by maybe population concerns,” he said. “Two of the key ingredients for a data centre or an artificial intelligence centre are land and power, and we know we’ve got a lot of those in the Mid West and the North West. That’s why they’re starting to attract some attention from proponents.”

Former Qantas workers who were illegally sacked five years ago have finally received their court-ordered payouts from a multimillion-dollar fine imposed on the airline, after a prolonged process that drew the ire of victims and the court. World.title: Australia to opt out of social media algorithms, Albanese confirms
World.content:
Australians over the age of 16 would be able to opt out of social media algorithms under new legislation cracking down on pornography and the glorification of crime, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has confirmed.

“We’ll require social media platforms to provide user empowerment tools that give people over the age of 16 genuine and enduring choice about what they see in their feeds,” Albanese told reporters in Canberra.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese unveiling the social media reforms in Canberra on Tuesday. Alex Ellinghausen

“It gives users choice, and it will hold the big tech companies responsible for inaction. If they don’t follow our laws, they will face significant penalties of more than $100 million.”

Labor released the first draft of its Digital Duty of Care laws on Tuesday. Communications Minister Anika Wells said the changes would allow people to choose between having an algorithm-defined social media feed or to just see “their friends, and the content creators they’ve chosen to follow”.

World.title: Spider-Man sinks Titanic: Inside the highest-grossing movies ever
World.content:
CultureMoviesBox office Spider-Man sinks Titanic: Inside the highest-grossing movies ever Nell Geraets September 8, 2026 — 12:22pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Spider-Man has overcome the Green Goblin, Doc Ock and Venom, but his latest triumph over Titanic could be his most memorable yet. Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which landed in theatres on July 31, has now sunk James Cameron’s beloved classic, shifting the 1997 film from the top five highest-grossing movies at the global box office. Titanic enjoyed a spot in the top five for nearly three decades, even topping the list for 12 years before being dethroned in 2010. Since then, Titanic has plunged further down the rankings, even with re-releases. Now, thanks to Spidey, it’s out of the top five entirely. Spider-Man: Brand New Day swung into the top five highest-grossing movies of all time, sinking Titanic along the way. Sony/AP Granted, this doesn’t take inflation into account. Most top five lists consider the actual money accumulated at the time each movie was released (as well as revenue from any re-releases). Movie tickets were far cheaper when Titanic hit screens, so more contemporary blockbusters are bound to earn more. On an inflation-adjusted list, classics such as Gone with the Wind, Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope and The Sound of Music would quickly climb the ranks. Regardless, with Titanic now off the top handful, which films remain? Here’s a rundown of the five films that have made the most money around the world.



5. Ne Zha 2 This Chinese fantasy animation is the highest-grossing non-English language film in history. It proved incredibly popular in China, becoming the first film ever to take more than $US1 billion ($1.38 billion) in a single territory. However, its popularity expanded far beyond China. In Australia, it made its debut as the third-highest ranking feature at the local box office. By its second weekend, it had made $5.22 million. Though much of Ne Zha 2’s success can be attributed to love for the original film, as well as its emotional depth in storytelling and stunning visual effects, there were also reports of the film being boosted by Chinese patriotism and a social media campaign. Fans encouraged others online to watch the film in cinemas multiple times. Chinese companies also got on board, including snacks manufacturer Weilong Food, which paused operations to take 900 of its employees to see the movie.



4. Avatar: The Way of Water Cameron blew audiences out of the water with Avatar in 2009, but his sequel to the sci-fi epic threw them right back into it. Avatar: The Way of Water once again lured people back to the cinema to see the awe-inspiring visuals on the biggest screen possible (and, of course, in 3D). Cameron even developed entirely new technology to record actors performing in live action underwater. The long-awaited sequel brought back fan favourites such as Zoe Saldaña and Sigourney Weaver, but it also introduced new major names such as Kate Winslet. Everything these actors’ characters did on screen, the actors actually performed in real life, with the crew logging about 200,000 hours of free-diving. Winslet even smashed Tom Cruise’s previous record for longest-held breath, and held hers for a staggering seven minutes and 14 seconds (Cruise held his breath for just over six minutes in Mission: Impossible – Rogue Nation). This brought an incredible air of authenticity and craft to the film, which evidently generated significant word-of-mouth. 3. Spider-Man: Brand New Day



Tom Holland’s successful run as Peter Parker continued with Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which has just enjoyed its sixth consecutive weekend atop the global box office. The film, directed by Dustin Daniel Cretton, hearkened back to Spider-Man’s roots, dropping Parker into the streets of New York where small-time criminals run amok. This return clearly paid off – the movie is currently experiencing the longest stint at No.1 since Avatar: The Way of Water in 2022. And according to Variety, Cretton’s movie is also primed to overtake Star Wars: The Force Awakens (2015) as the highest-grossing movie of all time at the US box office. These figures helped the Marvel film to not only bump Titanic – a cinematic behemoth that had been in the top five for nearly as long as Holland has been alive – but it also completely re-shuffled the list by overtaking both Ne Zha 2 and the Avatar sequel. 2. Avengers: Endgame



Avengers: Endgame was the finale to end all finales. After about 23 Marvel films, the Infinity Saga wrapped up with this behemoth of a blockbuster, one that brought some of the most famous superheroes – including Captain America and the Hulk – against a truly remarkable villain, Thanos. The stakes could not have been higher, as major names within the Marvel Cinematic Universe were snuffed out, and the fate of half of humanity lay in the hands of those who remained. Of course people wanted to see this on the big screen. Endgame may even rise further up the box office ranks, given it’s to be re-released this month ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday in December. 1. Avatar Cameron’s Titanic may have been knocked from the top, but the renowned director still claims two of the coveted spots, including No.1.



Avatar fundamentally changed cinema in 2009. It pioneered advanced motion capture and revolutionised 3D technology, attracting audiences for the visual spectacle alone. This earned it a best picture nomination at the Academy Awards. While it may not have won in that category, it did pick up Oscars for best cinematography, visual effects and art direction. The film enjoyed the top spot for about a decade before being briefly surpassed by Endgame in 2019. However, an Avatar re-release in China the following year reversed that, and it has remained the world’s highest-grossing movie since. What about Star Wars?! None of the Star Wars films are currently in the top five (though if these lists accounted for inflation, Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope likely would). That said, one of the sci-fi epics – Star Wars: The Force Awakens – remains close to the top. Here are the five titles trailing the top five: 6. Titanic (1997) 7. Star Wars: The Force Awakens (2015) 8. Avengers: Infinity War (2018) 9. Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021) 10. Zootopia 2 (2025) Must-see movies, interviews and all the latest from the world of film delivered to your inbox.

Private schools Text messages emerge in Scots College rape case amid calls for principal’s resignation Writing for this masthead last month, sexual consent activist and Teach Us Consent founder and chief executive Chanel Contos said Lambert had ignored her attempts to share concerning testimonies from young women allegedly assaulted by former Scots students. The college has repeatedly refused to answer questions about the boys’ enrolment status, their future at the school, and what measures were being implemented at the Bellevue Hill campus in response to the charges. The college declined to answer questions related to the boys’ enrolment status on Tuesday.



The boys will return to court on October 20. World.title: Spider-Man sinks Titanic: Inside the highest-grossing movies ever
World.content:
CultureMoviesBox office Spider-Man sinks Titanic: Inside the highest-grossing movies ever Nell Geraets September 8, 2026 — 12:22pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Spider-Man has overcome the Green Goblin, Doc Ock and Venom, but his latest triumph over Titanic could be his most memorable yet. Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which landed in theatres on July 31, has now sunk James Cameron’s beloved classic, shifting the 1997 film from the top five highest-grossing movies at the global box office. Titanic enjoyed a spot in the top five for nearly three decades, even topping the list for 12 years before being dethroned in 2010. Since then, Titanic has plunged further down the rankings, even with re-releases. Now, thanks to Spidey, it’s out of the top five entirely. Spider-Man: Brand New Day swung into the top five highest-grossing movies of all time, sinking Titanic along the way. Sony/AP Granted, this doesn’t take inflation into account. Most top five lists consider the actual money accumulated at the time each movie was released (as well as revenue from any re-releases). Movie tickets were far cheaper when Titanic hit screens, so more contemporary blockbusters are bound to earn more. On an inflation-adjusted list, classics such as Gone with the Wind, Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope and The Sound of Music would quickly climb the ranks. Regardless, with Titanic now off the top handful, which films remain? Here’s a rundown of the five films that have made the most money around the world.



5. Ne Zha 2 This Chinese fantasy animation is the highest-grossing non-English language film in history. It proved incredibly popular in China, becoming the first film ever to take more than $US1 billion ($1.38 billion) in a single territory. However, its popularity expanded far beyond China. In Australia, it made its debut as the third-highest ranking feature at the local box office. By its second weekend, it had made $5.22 million. Though much of Ne Zha 2’s success can be attributed to love for the original film, as well as its emotional depth in storytelling and stunning visual effects, there were also reports of the film being boosted by Chinese patriotism and a social media campaign. Fans encouraged others online to watch the film in cinemas multiple times. Chinese companies also got on board, including snacks manufacturer Weilong Food, which paused operations to take 900 of its employees to see the movie.



4. Avatar: The Way of Water Cameron blew audiences out of the water with Avatar in 2009, but his sequel to the sci-fi epic threw them right back into it. Avatar: The Way of Water once again lured people back to the cinema to see the awe-inspiring visuals on the biggest screen possible (and, of course, in 3D). Cameron even developed entirely new technology to record actors performing in live action underwater. The long-awaited sequel brought back fan favourites such as Zoe Saldaña and Sigourney Weaver, but it also introduced new major names such as Kate Winslet. Everything these actors’ characters did on screen, the actors actually performed in real life, with the crew logging about 200,000 hours of free-diving. Winslet even smashed Tom Cruise’s previous record for longest-held breath, and held hers for a staggering seven minutes and 14 seconds (Cruise held his breath for just over six minutes in Mission: Impossible – Rogue Nation). This brought an incredible air of authenticity and craft to the film, which evidently generated significant word-of-mouth. 3. Spider-Man: Brand New Day



Tom Holland’s successful run as Peter Parker continued with Spider-Man: Brand New Day, which has just enjoyed its sixth consecutive weekend atop the global box office. The film, directed by Dustin Daniel Cretton, hearkened back to Spider-Man’s roots, dropping Parker into the streets of New York where small-time criminals run amok. This return clearly paid off – the movie is currently experiencing the longest stint at No.1 since Avatar: The Way of Water in 2022. And according to Variety, Cretton’s movie is also primed to overtake Star Wars: The Force Awakens (2015) as the highest-grossing movie of all time at the US box office. These figures helped the Marvel film to not only bump Titanic – a cinematic behemoth that had been in the top five for nearly as long as Holland has been alive – but it also completely re-shuffled the list by overtaking both Ne Zha 2 and the Avatar sequel. 2. Avengers: Endgame



Avengers: Endgame was the finale to end all finales. After about 23 Marvel films, the Infinity Saga wrapped up with this behemoth of a blockbuster, one that brought some of the most famous superheroes – including Captain America and the Hulk – against a truly remarkable villain, Thanos. The stakes could not have been higher, as major names within the Marvel Cinematic Universe were snuffed out, and the fate of half of humanity lay in the hands of those who remained. Of course people wanted to see this on the big screen. Endgame may even rise further up the box office ranks, given it’s to be re-released this month ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday in December. 1. Avatar Cameron’s Titanic may have been knocked from the top, but the renowned director still claims two of the coveted spots, including No.1.



Avatar fundamentally changed cinema in 2009. It pioneered advanced motion capture and revolutionised 3D technology, attracting audiences for the visual spectacle alone. This earned it a best picture nomination at the Academy Awards. While it may not have won in that category, it did pick up Oscars for best cinematography, visual effects and art direction. The film enjoyed the top spot for about a decade before being briefly surpassed by Endgame in 2019. However, an Avatar re-release in China the following year reversed that, and it has remained the world’s highest-grossing movie since. What about Star Wars?! None of the Star Wars films are currently in the top five (though if these lists accounted for inflation, Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope likely would). That said, one of the sci-fi epics – Star Wars: The Force Awakens – remains close to the top. Here are the five titles trailing the top five: 6. Titanic (1997) 7. Star Wars: The Force Awakens (2015) 8. Avengers: Infinity War (2018) 9. Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021) 10. World.title: El Niño impacts on Pacific forecast to last well into 2027
World.content:
The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) says the intensifying El Niño phase will bring exceptionally warm tropical Pacific Ocean conditions in the coming months.

In its latest update, the WMO says El Niño is already causing disruption and devastation from droughts and floods in various parts of thre world including the Pacific, and is expected to peak towards the end of this year, with climate impacts continuing well into 2027.

A number of Pacific countries have been experiencing severe drought conditions as a result of the weather pattern.

Data released by the WMO shows a significant build up of smoke from Indonesian forest fires, including in South Papua province, has crossed borders into neighbouring countries including Papua New Guinea and Malaysia.

As the WMO advises regional countries to pay extra heed to weather forecasts and services, the UN Secretary-General António Guterres issued a warning.

He said the science leaves no room for doubt that the planet is in uncharted waters, and that those waters are heating up.

Guterres said sea surface temperatures are rising, stressing that the world is in the danger zone of extreme weather.

Woolworths supermarket is recalling one of its own cereals due to the potential presence of plastic.

Screengrab
